title_en: Trump effectively ended asylum. Advocates look to the Supreme Court to restore it
title_zh: 特朗普实际上结束了庇护。支持者希望最高法院恢复它
summary: Trump's sweeping immigration changes — an asylum ban, mass firings and new legal maneuvers — have all but ended asylum. The high court will soon consider whether some shifts deny people due process.
summary_zh: 特朗普全面的移民改革——庇护禁令、大规模解雇和新的法律举措——几乎结束了庇护。高等法院将很快考虑
body_en: Asylum denials have soared in Trump's second term : NPR

Asylum denials have soared in Trump's second term Trump's sweeping immigration changes — an asylum ban, mass firings and new legal maneuvers — have all but ended asylum. The high court will soon consider whether some shifts deny people due process.

For nearly two years, the Trump administration has prohibited asylum claims at the U.S.-Mexico border, canceled thousands of pending asylum applications and overhauled the immigration court system with mass firings. Critics say that combined, these moves have effectively shut down a once vital pathway for those fleeing persecution or danger.
The U.S. Supreme Court will soon consider whether the president can circumvent Congress and existing federal immigration law and unilaterally suspend access to asylum protections.

The legal challenge to the president's ban , which went into effect within hours of President Trump retaking office, is the latest legal case against the administration's seismic immigration policy changes that will be taken up by the high court. Those policy changes, critics say, have robbed asylum seekers of basic due process rights and have transformed the immigration court system into a deportation arm of Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE).

In legal filings, the Trump administration has insisted the proclamation is a necessary protection against "invasion" along the southern border and what the president and conservative critics have long said is abuse of the system by "fake" asylum seekers. Since it has been in place, the chaotic crush of people crossing into the U.S. has plummeted. U.S. Border Patrol apprehensions dropped to their lowest level in agency history this year. The agency recorded fewer than 99,000 Southwest border apprehensions in fiscal year 2026 — a 95% decline compared with more than 1.8 million per year under President Biden, according to U.S. Customs and Border Protection data .

"The difference between an average month under Trump and an average month under Biden is just staggering," Simon Hankinson, a senior research fellow with the Border Security and Immigration Center at the Heritage Foundation, a conservative think tank closely aligned with Trump, told NPR. And should the Supreme Court reverse the ban, "it would be disastrous," he added.

Hankinson contends that most people arriving at the southern border don't qualify for asylum. "And even if they did, they've already passed through Mexico, which is a safe third country where they could claim asylum, especially if they're coming from Venezuela or Afghanistan. So you have a population that overwhelmingly will not qualify under U.S. law for asylum. They're here because they want to get a job," he said.
But, critics say, taken together the administration's moves have gutted access to asylum.

Despite newly restored quiet along the southern border, the president's argument for the asylum ban has been rejected by two lower federal courts. It has, however, remained largely in place as the case is tied up in court battles.

In December, the Supreme Court will review the administration's strategy of deporting immigrants to third countries that have agreed to adjudicate asylum claims, even as some of those countries face human rights abuse allegations and cannot guarantee that the person seeking asylum won't be returned to their home nation.
The administration faces a third legal battle that could end its attempt to indefinitely detain thousands of people in deportation proceedings.

If the majority-conservative court rules in favor of immigrant advocates in the lawsuits, advocates say, the decisions could finally break the choke hold that the Trump administration has had on asylum approvals, which are at their lowest in decades. National asylum denial rates soared to 94% in June , up from about 50% in 2024 — the last full year of the Biden administration. That's according to TRAC, a research project at Syracuse University that tracks data about immigration judges.

"The president does not have the right to unilaterally override the protections Congress has afforded those fleeing danger," said Lee Gelernt, lead counsel and deputy director of the Immigrants' Rights Project at the American Civil Liberties Union, one of the groups behind the challenge to the asylum ban. "The courts are right to reject this unprecedented power grab that would put countless lives in danger. We look forward to making our case before the Supreme Court."

Lawyers for migrants seeking asylum are hoping for wins at the high court. For several of Madhavi Narayanan's clients, this could be lifesaving. A Los Angeles-based immigration attorney with Human Rights First, she is currently representing immigrants who, prior to Trump's second term, would have had what she calls "slam dunk" asylum petitions.

One of them is a 30-something Ethiopian man called ZG, who arrived in the U.S. through Mexico in February 2025 after enduring extensive torture in his native country. Narayanan requested that NPR use only ZG because he fears retribution from the Ethiopian government. Upon turning himself in at the southern border, ZG was placed into detention and immediately filed an asylum petition.

Narayanan said ZG is a member of an Indigenous group in Ethiopia that's part of an ongoing armed conflict in that nation, which human rights organizations report is at risk of committing more atrocities against civilians . And, Narayanan, who has been working on the case for nine months, said she has produced documents and letters to support his claims of torture.

"Any other time, it would have been a really straightforward case," she said, adding that "there's a wide, wide range of human rights reports explaining that folks in this exact position would be at high risk" of violence and death if they were to return to Ethiopia.
body_zh: 特朗普第二任期内拒绝庇护的人数激增：NPR
在特朗普第二任期内，拒绝庇护的情况激增。特朗普全面的移民改革——庇护禁令、大规模解雇和新的法律举措——几乎结束了庇护。高等法院很快将考虑某些转变是否剥夺了人们的正当程序。
近两年来，特朗普政府禁止在美墨边境提出庇护申请，取消了数千份未决的庇护申请，并通过大规模解雇人员彻底改革了移民法院系统。批评人士表示，这些举措综合起来，有效地关闭了那些逃离迫害或危险的人曾经至关重要的通道。
美国最高法院很快将考虑总统是否可以规避国会和现行联邦移民法并单方面暂停获得庇护保护。
对总统禁令的法律挑战是在特朗普总统重新就任后几小时内生效的，这是针对政府重大移民政策变化的最新法律案件，将由高等法院审理。批评者称，这些政策变化剥夺了寻求庇护者的基本正当程序权利，并将移民法院系统转变为移民和海关执法局 (ICE) 的驱逐部门。

在法律文件中，特朗普政府坚称，该公告是防止南部边境“入侵”以及总统和保守派批评者长期以来所说的“假”寻求庇护者滥用该系统的必要保护措施。自从它实施以来，进入美国的混乱人群已经大幅减少。美国边境巡逻队今年的逮捕人数降至该机构历史上的最低水平。根据美国海关和边境保护局的数据，2026 财年，该机构在西南边境逮捕的人数不到 99,000 人，与拜登总统领导下每年超过 180 万人的逮捕人数相比下降了 95%。
与特朗普关系密切的保守派智库传统基金会边境安全和移民中心高级研究员西蒙·汉金森 (Simon Hankinson) 告诉 NPR，“特朗普领导下的平均一个月和拜登领导下的平均一个月之间的差异是惊人的。”他补充说，如果最高法院撤销该禁令，“那将是灾难性的”。
汉金森认为，大多数抵达南部边境的人没有资格获得庇护。 “即使他们这样做了，他们也已经通过了墨西哥，这是一个安全的第三国，他们可以在那里申请庇护，特别是如果他们来自委内瑞拉或阿富汗。所以，根据美国法律，绝大多数人不符合庇护资格。他们来这里是因为他们想找到工作，”他说。
但批评人士表示，综合来看，政府的举措已经削弱了获得庇护的机会。
尽管南部边境刚刚恢复平静，但总统关于庇护禁令的论点已被两个下级联邦法院驳回。然而，由于案件仍在法庭斗争中，它基本上仍然存在。
12月，最高法院将审查政府将移民驱逐到同意裁决庇护申请的第三国的策略，尽管其中一些国家面临侵犯人权的指控，并且不能保证寻求庇护的人不会被遣返回国。
政府面临第三场法律诉讼，这可能会结束其在驱逐程序中无限期拘留数千人的企图。
倡导者表示，如果保守派占多数的法院在诉讼中做出有利于移民倡导者的裁决，这些决定可能最终打破特朗普政府对庇护批准的阻碍，庇护批准处于几十年来的最低水平。 6 月份，全国庇护拒绝率飙升至 94%，高于 2024 年（拜登政府执政的最后一年）的约 50%。这是雪城大学追踪移民法官数据的研究项目 TRAC 得出的结论。
“总统无权单方面推翻国会为那些逃离危险的人提供的保护，”美国公民自由联盟移民权利项目的首席律师兼副主任李·格勒恩特说，该联盟是挑战庇护禁令的组织之一。 “法院驳回这种史无前例的权力争夺是正确的，这将使无数人的生命处于危险之中。我们期待着向最高法院提起诉讼。”
寻求庇护的移民律师希望在高等法院获胜。对于马达维·纳拉亚南 (Madhavi Narayanan) 的几位客户来说，这可能会挽救生命。她是人权第一组织驻洛杉矶的移民律师，目前代表那些在特朗普第二任期之前曾收到她所说的“灌篮式”庇护申请的移民。
其中一名 30 多岁的埃塞俄比亚男子名叫 ZG，他在祖国遭受了广泛的酷刑后于 2025 年 2 月经墨西哥抵达美国。纳拉亚南要求 NPR 仅使用 ZG，因为他担心埃塞俄比亚政府的报复。在南部边境自首后，ZG 被拘留并立即提交了庇护申请。
纳拉亚南说，ZG 是埃塞俄比亚一个土著群体的成员，该群体是该国持续武装冲突的一部分，人权组织报告称，该群体有可能对平民实施更多暴行。纳拉亚南已经处理此案九个月了，她说她已经出示了文件和信件来支持他遭受酷刑的说法。
“在其他时候，这将是一个非常简单的案件，”她说，并补充说，“有大量、广泛的人权报告解释说，处于这种情况的人如果返回埃塞俄比亚，将面临暴力和死亡的高风险”。

title_en: ‘Abusive and insulting to Canadians’: campaign to oust US ambassador presented to parliament
title_zh: “辱骂和侮辱加拿大人”：向议会提出驱逐美国大使的运动
summary: Hundreds of thousands of Canadians call for Pete Hoekstra to be declared ‘persona non grata’ A petition signed by nearly 290,000 Canadians calling on Mark Carney’s government to oust Pete Hoekstra as US ambassador to Canada was formally presented to the House
summary_zh: 数十万加拿大人呼吁将皮特·霍克斯特拉 (Pete Hoekstra) 列为“不受欢迎的人” 近 29 万加拿大人签署的请愿书呼吁
body_en: Hundreds of thousands of Canadians call for Pete Hoekstra to be declared ‘persona non grata’

A petition signed by nearly 290,000 Canadians calling on Mark Carney’s government to oust Pete Hoekstra as US ambassador to Canada was formally presented to the House of Commons on Thursday, a sign of the strained relations between the neighboring countries.

Elizabeth May, a Canadian Green party member, originally opened the petition for signatures in July 2026 after a woman from Calgary sponsored it. The petition requests that the Canadian government declare Hoekstra “persona non grata” due to his “US” diplomatic interference in Canadian domestic affairs”.
US ambassador suggests Trump could blame Canada if midterms don’t go his way
“He has been repeatedly abusive and insulting to Canadians,” May said as she formally introduced the petition, according to Politico .
She called Donald Trump’s envoy “the most undiplomatic diplomat” Canada had ever seen.
The petition accuses Hoekstra of “undermining” Canada-US diplomatic relations through repeated statements about Canadian politics that its signatories say are “inconsistent with diplomatic protocol”.
The US state department said it was aware of the petition.
Hoekstra is a deeply polarizing figure in Canada, particularly for his response to Trump’s desire to annex the country and make Canada the 51st US state.

Speaking to a Michigan radio station last year, he described the president’s rhetoric as a “sign of affection” and questioned why Canadians were offended by what he characterized as a “generous offer”.
Hoekstra also previously described Canada’s 2025 federal election that saw a remarkable come-from-behind victory for the prime minister’s Liberal party as “anti-American”.
The US ambassador had suggested Canada could be blamed if Republicans performed poorly in this month’s midterm elections.
“That’s an interesting way of framing it,” Carney replied, when asked about the comments.
Democrats swept the November elections, including key Senate races in border states such as Michigan and Maine, where the bitter tariff war between Washington and Ottawa has hit residents hard.
Last month Carney said American tariffs hurt both American and Canadian households. He added that auto exports to the US had so far fallen 10%, and US exports to Canada have fallen by more than 20%.

“US tariffs have upended a trade bargain that’s existed for decades,” Carney said. “They’ve raised costs for American families while putting Ontario workers and businesses at a disadvantage and under a cloud of uncertainty.”

Hoekstra had also accused Canada of potential “political interference” in the US election, a claim Carney said held “no merit”. Speaking to reporters in Turkey, the prime minister said he was “disappointed that their envoy sees that as his role, to make these suggestions”.
Even though the Canadian government is required to provide a formal response to the petition presented by May, the petition is nonbinding.
“I think the government will quite likely say, ‘No, we’re not prepared to declare Pete Hoekstra persona non grata and strip him of his diplomatic credentials,’”, May said in an interview with CTV .
body_zh: 数十万加拿大人呼吁宣布皮特·霍克斯特拉为“不受欢迎的人”
周四，一份由近 29 万加拿大人签署的请愿书正式提交给下议院，呼吁马克·卡尼政府罢免美国驻加拿大大使皮特·霍克斯特拉，这表明邻国之间关系紧张。
加拿大绿党成员伊丽莎白·梅 (Elizabeth May) 最初于 2026 年 7 月在一位来自卡尔加里的女性的赞助下开放了请愿书以征集签名。请愿书要求加拿大政府宣布霍克斯特拉为“不受欢迎的人”，因为他的“美国”对加拿大内政的外交干涉”。
美国大使表示，如果中期选举不顺利，特朗普可能会责怪加拿大
据《Politico》报道，梅在正式介绍请愿书时说道：“他一再辱骂和侮辱加拿大人。”
她称唐纳德·特朗普的特使是加拿大有史以来“最不外交的外交官”。
请愿书指责霍克斯特拉反复发表有关加拿大政治的言论，“破坏”加美外交关系，请愿书签署者称这些言论“不符合外交礼仪”。
美国国务院表示已获悉该请愿书。
霍克斯特拉在加拿大是一个两极分化严重的人物，尤其是他对特朗普吞并加拿大并使加拿大成为美国第 51 个州的愿望的回应。
去年，他在密歇根一家广播电台发表讲话时，将总统的言论描述为“感情的表现”，并质疑为什么加拿大人会因为他所说的“慷慨的提议”而感到冒犯。
霍克斯特拉此前还将加拿大2025年联邦大选描述为“反美”，这场选举中总理所在的自由党取得了令人瞩目的逆转胜利。
美国大使曾表示，如果共和党在本月的中期选举中表现不佳，加拿大可能会受到指责。
当被问及这些评论时，卡尼回答道：“这是一种有趣的表达方式。”
民主党在 11 月份的选举中大获全胜，包括密歇根州和缅因州等边境州的关键参议院竞选，华盛顿和渥太华之间激烈的关税战对这些州的居民造成了沉重打击。
卡尼上个月表示，美国的关税伤害了美国和加拿大的家庭。他补充说，迄今为止，美国对美国的汽车出口下降了10%，美国对加拿大的出口下降了20%以上。
卡尼表示：“美国的关税颠覆了存在了数十年的贸易协议。” “他们提高了美国家庭的成本，同时使安大略省的工人和企业处于不利地位并处于不确定性的阴云之下。”
霍克斯特拉还指责加拿大可能对美国大选进行“政治干预”，卡尼称这一说法“毫无根据”。总理在土耳其对记者表示，他“对他们的特使将提出这些建议视为他的职责感到失望”。
尽管加拿大政府被要求对梅提交的请愿书做出正式回应，但该请愿书不具有约束力。
“我认为政府很可能会说，‘不，我们不准备宣布皮特·霍克斯特拉为不受欢迎的人并剥夺他的外交证件，’”梅在接受 CTV 采访时表示。

title_en: Sales for Biden memoir fall far short of books by Obama and Clinton
title_zh: 拜登回忆录的销量远远低于奥巴马和克林顿的书籍
summary: Promise Me, America, which has lukewarm reviews from critics, sold about 21,000 copies during its first week on sale Joe Biden’s memoir Promise Me, America debuted with modest sales and lackluster reviews, selling about 21,000 copies during its first week on s
summary_zh: 《答应我，美国》受到评论家的冷淡评价，在发售第一周就售出了约 21,000 册乔·拜登的回忆录《答应我，美国》
body_en: Promise Me, America, which has lukewarm reviews from critics, sold about 21,000 copies during its first week on sale
Joe Biden’s memoir Promise Me, America debuted with modest sales and lackluster reviews, selling about 21,000 copies during its first week on sale, according to Circana.
It sold well enough to top the New York Times nonfiction bestseller list, but didn’t approach the level of memoirs by such predecessors as Barack Obama and Bill Clinton .
Circana, an American market research and data analytics firm, tracks about 85% of the physical books market.

Promise Me, America published last week, receiving lukewarm reviews. Critics found the book mostly unrevealing about Biden’s time in office and about his decision in 2024 not to run again amid widespread concern about his age and health. A New York Times review was headlined “Reflecting on 2024, Joe Biden Finds No Faults of His Own.”
Promise Me, America by Joe Biden review – former president defends his decisions
Sales may also have suffered from the 84-year-old Biden’s limited promotion for the book; he is battling stage 4 prostate cancer.

By comparison, Obama’s A Promised Land sold more than 800,000 copies within 24 hours of going on sale in 2020 and topped 1m by the end of the week. Clinton’s My Life, released in 2004, topped 1m sales within the first two weeks.

Books by and about the Bidens have in general attracted less interest than books about other presidential families. Former first lady Jill Biden’s View from the East Wing, published in June, has sold approximately 46,000 copies according to Circana. By comparison, White House memoirs by Michelle Obama and Hillary Clinton were both million sellers within a month of their release.
The book’s publisher, Little, Brown and Company, released a statement saying they were “immensely proud” of it topping the New York Times nonfiction bestseller list.
body_zh: 《答应我，美国》受到评论家的冷淡评价，在发售第一周就售出了约 21,000 本
据 Circana 称，乔·拜登的回忆录《答应我，美国》首映销量平平，评论也乏善可陈，发售第一周就售出约 21,000 册。
它的销量很好，在《纽约时报》非小说类畅销书排行榜上名列前茅，但还没有达到巴拉克·奥巴马和比尔·克林顿等前辈回忆录的水平。
Circana 是一家美国市场研究和数据分析公司，追踪约 85% 的实体书市场。
《答应我，美国》上周出版，但反响冷淡。批评者发现，这本书大多没有透露拜登的执政时间，以及他在 2024 年因年龄和健康状况普遍担忧而决定不再参选的信息。 《纽约时报》一篇评论的标题是“反思 2024 年，乔·拜登没有发现自己的任何错误”。
乔·拜登评论《答应我，美国》——前总统捍卫他的决定
84 岁的拜登对这本书的宣传有限，也可能影响了销量。他正在与第四期前列腺癌作斗争。
相比之下，奥巴马的《应许之地》在 2020 年上市后 24 小时内售出超过 80 万份，到周末销量突破 100 万份。克林顿的《我的生活》于 2004 年发行，发行后两周内销量突破 100 万份。
总的来说，拜登家族的书籍和有关拜登家族的书籍比有关其他总统家族的书籍引起的兴趣要少。据 Circana 报道，前第一夫人吉尔·拜登的《东翼景观》于 6 月出版，已售出约 46,000 册。相比之下，米歇尔·奥巴马和希拉里·克林顿的白宫回忆录在发行后一个月内销量均突破百万。
该书的出版商利特尔布朗公司发表声明称，他们对这本书荣登《纽约时报》非小说类畅销书榜首感到“非常自豪”。

title_en: Three studies link glyphosate to cancer, contradicting claims of Trump EPA
title_zh: 三项研究将草甘膦与癌症联系起来，与特朗普环保署的说法相矛盾
summary: Experts say NIH research raises concerns about chemical companies’ influence on US agency’s pesticide division The US government’s top medical research agency has released three new studies linking glyphosate, the world’s most widely used pesticide and an acti
summary_zh: 专家表示，NIH的研究引发了人们对化学公司对美国机构农药部门影响的担忧 美国政府最高医学研究
body_en: Experts say NIH research raises concerns about chemical companies’ influence on US agency’s pesticide division

The US government’s top medical research agency has released three new studies linking glyphosate, the world’s most widely used pesticide and an active ingredient in Roundup, to cancer . The National Institutes of Health (NIH) findings contradict a controversial recent Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) conclusion that the weedkiller is not a carcinogen, and deals a blow to the White House, which has been closely allied with Roundup’s producer, Bayer.

The NIH’s three papers could have significant political and legal fallout. The EPA is in the process of a court-ordered re-evaluation of glyphosate’s cancer risks. The NIH findings generate new pressure for the EPA to find that the substance is linked to cancer, which would subject it to a modest increase in regulations.

If the EPA again finds that glyphosate is not carcinogenic, the NIH studies would complicate the legal terrain for it and Bayer. The papers also represent a major public relations hit for Bayer, which has relentlessly defended the herbicide, for which it recorded $2.8bn in sales in 2024.

Nathan Donley, environmental health science director at the Center for Biological Diversity, said the studies raised further questions about chemical companies’ influence on the EPA’s pesticide division , which “parrots industry talking points” in its safety reviews.

“Americans would be smart to heed the cancer findings of the nation’s most trusted scientific institution rather than the industry-influenced claims of the EPA,” Donley said. “The EPA’s pesticide office has made a mockery of pesticide science for far too long.”
The EPA did not respond to a request for comment.

In a statement, Ruveon, a Bayer subsidiary that manages Roundup in the US, said in a statement: “The US EPA, like other leading health authorities globally, has previously and repeatedly concluded that glyphosate does not cause cancer.”

The NIH findings arrive during a year in which the White House has come under fire from across the political spectrum for its support for Bayer. That includes an executive order from Donald Trump that aimed to protect the substance’s production and provide immunity to its producers, and an amicus brief in support of Bayer in an eventual US supreme court case that partially shielded the company from lawsuits.

The NIH did not carry out new studies, but conducted a systematic review of decades of scientific literature from across the globe. It found an association with blood cancers in humans, and that the pesticide caused several types of tumors in animals.

Advocates say the NIH used proper scientific protocol, which is followed by the World Health Organization’s International Agency on Research for Cancer (IARC), and other credible research organizations.

The EPA’s pesticide division reviewed most of the same studies several years ago but came to a different conclusion because it deviated from its own methodology, Donley said. A court threw out the EPA’s findings in 2022 because it did not use proper protocol, and ordered a new risk assessment.

The EPA is expected to finish it early next year, Donley said. The EPA and NIH are often aligned on many chemicals’ risk assessments, but the pesticide division chronically underestimates cancer risks because of its flawed methodology, he added.
“This agency is completely incapable of doing a good, clear, robust cancer assessment, not just with glyphosate, but all pesticides, because they don’t follow their own methodology,” Donley said.

The administration’s support for glyphosate has driven a wedge between pro-industry figures in the White House, and the Make America Healthy Again (Maha) movement, which the health secretary, Robert F Kennedy Jr, spearheads.

Kelly Ryerson, a Maha advocate who has met with top agency officials to advocate for stricter pesticide policies, told the Guardian she is “extremely hopeful that glyphosate’s day of reckoning has arrived”.

“The release of the government-performed studies on glyphosate further prove what many independent scientists have claimed for decades: glyphosate can cause cancer. The EPA will be forced to change its determination of carcinogenicity in the upcoming review,” Ryerson said.

She noted the NIH papers are in addition to a recent US Department of Health and Human Services-commissioned study that similarly reviewed literature on glyphosate’s impact on hormones and found it probably reduced sperm counts and testosterone.
Donley said he is “99.9% certain the EPA is going to again find that glyphosate does not cause cancer”.
body_zh: 专家表示，美国国立卫生研究院的研究引发了人们对化学公司对美国机构农药部门影响的担忧
美国政府最高医学研究机构发布了三项新研究，将世界上使用最广泛的农药和农达的活性成分草甘膦与癌症联系起来。美国国立卫生研究院 (NIH) 的调查结果与环境保护署 (EPA) 最近得出的一项有争议的结论相矛盾，即除草剂不是致癌物，这对与农达生产商拜耳 (Bayer) 关系密切的白宫造成了打击。
美国国立卫生研究院的三篇论文可能会产生重大的政治和法律影响。美国环保署正在法院下令重新评估草甘膦的癌症风险。美国国立卫生研究院的调查结果给美国环保局带来了新的压力，要求其发现该物质与癌症有关，这将使其受到适度增加的监管。
如果美国环保局再次发现草甘膦不致癌，美国国立卫生研究院的研究将使该公司和拜耳的法律领域变得更加复杂。这些论文还对拜耳的公关造成了重大打击，该公司一直不懈地为这款除草剂辩护，该除草剂在 2024 年的销售额达到了 28 亿美元。
生物多样性中心环境健康科学主任内森·唐利表示，这些研究进一步引发了人们对化学公司对美国环保局农药部门影响的质疑，该部门在其安全审查中“鹦鹉学舌地重复行业话题”。
唐利说：“美国人应该明智地关注美国最值得信赖的科学机构的癌症发现，而不是美国环保署受行业影响的主张。” “美国环保署农药办公室嘲笑农药科学太久了。”
美国环保署没有回应置评请求。
负责管理农达在美国的拜耳子公司 Ruveon 在一份声明中表示：“美国环保署与全球其他主要卫生当局一样，此前曾多次得出草甘膦不会致癌的结论。”
美国国立卫生研究院的调查结果发布之际，白宫因其对拜耳的支持而受到来自各个政治派别的批评。其中包括唐纳德·特朗普的一项行政命令，旨在保护该物质的生产并为其生产者提供豁免权，以及在最终的美国最高法院案件中支持拜耳的法庭之友简报，该案件部分保护了该公司免受诉讼。
美国国立卫生研究院没有开展新的研究，而是对全球数十年的科学文献进行了系统回顾。研究发现该杀虫剂与人类血癌有关，并且该杀虫剂会导致动物出现多种类型的肿瘤。
支持者称，美国国立卫生研究院使用了正确的科学方案，世界卫生组织的国际癌症研究机构（IARC）和其他可靠的研究组织也遵循该方案。
唐利说，美国环保局农药部门几年前审查了大部分相同的研究，但得出了不同的结论，因为它偏离了自己的方法。法院于 2022 年驳回了 EPA 的调查结果，因为它没有使用适当的协议，并下令进行新的风险评估。
唐利说，美国环保局预计将于明年初完成这项工作。他补充说，美国环保局和美国国立卫生研究院在许多化学品的风险评估上经常保持一致，但农药部门由于其方法存在缺陷，长期低估癌症风险。
唐利说：“该机构完全无法对草甘膦以及所有农药进行良好、清晰、稳健的癌症评估，因为他们不遵循自己的方法。”
政府对草甘膦的支持在白宫的亲工业人士和卫生部长小罗伯特·F·肯尼迪(Robert F Kennedy Jr.)带头的“让美国再次健康”(Maha)运动之间产生了分歧。
马哈倡导者凯利·瑞尔森（Kelly Ryerson）曾与高级机构官员会面，倡导更严格的农药政策，她告诉《卫报》，她“非常希望草甘膦的清算日已经到来”。
“政府对草甘膦进行的研究的发布进一步证明了许多独立科学家几十年来所声称的：草甘膦会致癌。美国环保署将被迫在即将进行的审查中改变其致癌性的确定，”瑞尔森说。
她指出，美国国立卫生研究院的论文是美国卫生与公众服务部最近委托的一项研究的补充，该研究同样回顾了有关草甘膦对激素影响的文献，发现它可能会减少精子数量和睾酮水平。
唐利表示，他“99.9% 确信 EPA 将再次发现草甘膦不会致癌”。

title_en: Trump Medicaid cuts will hit the most vulnerable Americans, officials say
title_zh: 官员称特朗普医疗补助削减将打击最脆弱的美国人
summary: In Kentucky, one of America’s unhealthiest states, denial of healthcare and potential closure of hospitals may affect 250,000 people The coalfields of eastern Kentucky fueled America’s economic rise in the early 20th century. But the state has since found itse
summary_zh: 在美国最不健康的州之一肯塔基州，拒绝提供医疗服务和医院可能关闭可能会影响 25 万人。
body_en: In Kentucky, one of America’s unhealthiest states, denial of healthcare and potential closure of hospitals may affect 250,000 people

The coalfields of eastern Kentucky fueled America’s economic rise in the early 20th century. But the state has since found itself left behind. A lack of investments in rural regions has triggered health and socioeconomic issues that have lingered for generations.

Today, Kentucky faces the third-highest cancer and third-highest drug overdose death rate in the country and is one of the top five worst-affected states in several other health metrics. It has come to rely heavily on federal healthcare assistance, with about 1.4 million people in Kentucky receiving Medicaid support.
But now, those issues are set to be further compounded by cuts to Medicaid enacted by the Trump administration that could directly affect up to 250,000 Kentucky residents.
About 35 rural Kentucky hospitals are believed to be at risk of closing as a result of the cuts, more than any other state.

“These hospitals are very dependent on Medicaid; it makes up a really significant part of the economy, particularly in eastern Kentucky. If you look at just Medicaid payments to providers in Kentucky’s fifth congressional district [a region encompassing much of Appalachian Kentucky], those payments make up 13.5% of the GDP there,” says Dustin Pugel, policy director at the Kentucky Center for Economic Policy, a research organization.

“That’s an enormous percent[age] of a regional economy. If that money starts to dry up either because people aren’t covered any more or through cuts to provider rates, that’s going to create enormous economic harm in those areas.”

Almost 36% of residents in Perry county in the south-east of Kentucky, including more than half of all children, relied on Medicaid in 2023 according to reports , a rate that’s 16% higher than the national level. At more than $10,600 per capita in 2023, Kentucky has some of the highest Medicaid expenses in the country.

The federal work requirement , in which many Americans must demonstrate they work or volunteer at least 80 hours a month in order to receive Medicaid support, comes into effect in January. Those who can’t submit records of hours worked or school attendance every six months will lose access from 2028. On top of that, reports suggests Kentucky is set to lose $28bn in federal Medicaid funding over the next decade.

Kentucky’s most vulnerable are set to be especially affected by the cuts. Local health centers, urgent care facilities and substance use disorder clinics that rely on federal funding to keep their doors open could face an untenable future.

“When you have five hospitals [in Appalachian Kentucky] that are at risk of closing, you have to take patients from an additional nine or 10 counties. It’s going to overwhelm the hospital that’s here,” says Zack Hall, chair of the Perry county Democratic party.
“You already have a situation in eastern Kentucky where most counties don’t have a hospital.”
Hall says the two areas in Appalachian Kentucky that need a higher rate of healthcare have issues with cancer and black lung, which are harder on the elderly population.
“If you are having to take an elderly patient and bring them to the hospital and having to drive two, two and a half hours to get them to a hospital, that makes it that much harder on them,” he says.
It stands to affect economies, not just individuals.

“In some of these counties, over two-thirds of their residents are covered by Medicaid . If they start losing coverage, particularly where there isn’t a lot of jobs – where people aren’t able to adhere to the work requirement or don’t have broadband so reporting their [work or volunteering] hours is difficult, you’re looking at a really significant economic headwind,” says Pugel. “That will certainly result in layoffs, may result in hospital closures and will definitely hurt people’s health.”

Before the Trump administration shut down the refugee resettlement program to all but white South Africans last year, Kentucky ranked fourth nationally in refugee resettlements per capita, according to the Immigration Research Initiative.
Without immigration, which numbered nearly 82,000 people between 2020 and 2025, Kentucky would have seen its population decline.

But since last month, refugees and asylees, who have played an important role in revitalizing small Kentuckian communities in recent years, have lost access to Medicaid, because of Trump’s One Big Beautiful Bill Act.
body_zh: 在美国最不健康的州之一肯塔基州，拒绝提供医疗服务和医院可能关闭可能会影响 25 万人
肯塔基州东部的煤田推动了 20 世纪初美国的经济崛起。但此后国家发现自己落在了后面。农村地区缺乏投资引发了几代人挥之不去的健康和社会经济问题。
如今，肯塔基州面临着全国第三高的癌症和第三高的药物过量死亡率，并且在其他几个健康指标中是受影响最严重的五个州之一。它已经严重依赖联邦医疗援助，肯塔基州约有 140 万人接受医疗补助支持。
但现在，特朗普政府削减医疗补助计划可能会直接影响多达 25 万肯塔基州居民，这些问题将进一步复杂化。
据信，肯塔基州约有 35 家乡村医院因削减开支而面临关闭的风险，比其他任何州都多。
“这些医院非常依赖医疗补助；它构成了经济的一个非常重要的组成部分，特别是在肯塔基州东部。如果你只看肯塔基州第五国会选区（涵盖阿巴拉契亚肯塔基州大部分地区）的医疗补助提供者的支付情况，这些付款占那里 GDP 的 13.5%，”研究机构肯塔基州经济政策中心的政策主任达斯汀·普格尔 (Dustin Pugel) 说。
“这在区域经济中占据了巨大的比例。如果这些资金开始枯竭，要么是因为人们不再得到保险，要么是由于医疗服务提供者费率的削减，这将给这些地区造成巨大的经济损害。”
据报道，到 2023 年，肯塔基州东南部佩里县近 36% 的居民（包括一半以上的儿童）依赖医疗补助，这一比例比全国水平高出 16%。到 2023 年，肯塔基州的人均医疗补助支出将超过 10,600 美元，位居全国最高。
联邦工作要求将于 1 月生效，其中许多美国人必须证明他们每月工作或志愿工作至少 80 小时才能获得医疗补助支持。那些无法每六个月提交一次工作时间或上学记录的人将从 2028 年起失去访问权限。除此之外，报告显示肯塔基州将在未来 10 年损失 280 亿美元的联邦医疗补助资金。
肯塔基州最弱势群体将尤其受到削减的影响。依靠联邦资金维持营业的当地卫生中心、紧急护理设施和药物滥用障碍诊所可能面临难以维持的未来。
“当（阿巴拉契亚肯塔基州）有五家医院面临关闭风险时，你必须从另外九个或十个县接收病人。这将使这里的医院不堪重负，”佩里县民主党主席扎克·霍尔（Zack Hall）说。
“在肯塔基州东部，大多数县都没有医院。”
霍尔说，肯塔基州阿巴拉契亚山脉的两个需要较高医疗保健率的地区存在癌症和黑肺问题，这对老年人来说更加困难。
“如果你必须带着一位老年患者去医院，并且必须开车两个、两个半小时才能将他们送到医院，这对他们来说就更加困难，”他说。
它不仅会影响个人，还会影响经济。
“在其中一些县，超过三分之二的居民享受医疗补助。如果他们开始失去医疗补助，特别是在没有很多工作机会的地方，人们无法遵守工作要求或没有宽带，因此报告他们的[工作或志愿服务]时间很困难，那么你就会看到真正重大的经济逆风，”普格尔说。 “这肯定会导致裁员，可能导致医院关闭，并且肯定会损害人们的健康。”
根据移民研究计划，在去年特朗普政府关闭除南非白人之外的所有人的难民安置计划之前，肯塔基州的人均难民安置数量在全国排名第四。
如果没有移民（2020 年至 2025 年间移民人数接近 82,000 人），肯塔基州的人口将会下降。
但自上个月以来，近年来在振兴肯塔基州小社区方面发挥重要作用的难民和政治庇护者，由于特朗普的《一项美丽的法案》而失去了获得医疗补助的机会。

title_en: Trump administration proposes new tariffs on goods from major U.S. trading partners
title_zh: 特朗普政府提议对美国主要贸易伙伴的商品征收新关税
summary: President Trump's new proposed tariffs are already meeting pushback from Democrats and some free trade advocates.
summary_zh: 特朗普总统提出的新关税已经遭到民主党和一些自由贸易倡导者的抵制。
body_en: Trump administration proposes new tariffs on goods from major U.S. trading partners President Trump's new proposed tariffs are already meeting pushback from Democrats and some free trade advocates.
President Trump's new proposed tariffs are already meeting pushback from Democrats and some free trade advocates.

The Trump administration is proposing new tariffs on goods from 14 of the U.S.'s biggest trading partners, including Japan, the EU and China. It's arguing that these new tariffs fight other countries' unfair trade practices, but it's not clear that they will actually do that.
For more, we have NPR White House correspondent Danielle Kurtzleben. Danielle, what did the White House outline yesterday?

DANIELLE KURTZLEBEN, BYLINE: Well, it's new proposed tariffs on goods from major trading partners - the ones you mentioned, and also South Korea and Cambodia, for example. And the rates could go as high as 40% on Chinese goods, also 35% on goods from Vietnam and 20 or 25% on goods from other countries. They're also proposing additional tariffs on sugar and aircrafts from Brazil, and that would add to previous tariffs the U.S. imposed there.
MARTÍNEZ: When could these plans actually become real?

KURTZLEBEN: Well, they could go into effect within a couple of months. That's what U.S. Trade Ambassador Jamieson Greer said yesterday. Now, as for what the rates will be, well, that's still unclear, and that's because for each country, excepting those additional tariffs on Brazil, the White House has two rates they've listed - a proposed rate and a deal rate. To give an example, the tariff on China could be 20%. That's the deal rate. But depending in part on how ongoing discussions go, the rates on Chinese goods could go as high as 40%.
MARTÍNEZ: Forty percent. Now, yeah, the Supreme Court struck down some of Trump's earlier tariffs. So how is the White House legally justifying these new ones?

KURTZLEBEN: Well, these are being implemented under a law known for short as Section 301, which is meant to counter other countries' unfair trade practices. And so here the White House is alleging that these other countries have what's called structural excess capacity in various manufactured goods. And the administration has described this as when another country has policies that cause a good to be overproduced, which then distorts a global market for that good. And so those practices, according to the administration, can include all sorts of things, like labor practices, subsidies and tax breaks.

Now, the administration imposed other sweeping 301 tariffs earlier this year, and there's a lawsuit in process challenging those, with the key argument being that those tariffs were just way broader than the 301 law calls for.
MARTÍNEZ: Now, you mentioned a lawsuit. Could these new tariffs face similar legal challenges?

KURTZLEBEN: You know, they could. We'll see what happens. But I talked to Sara Albrecht. She's chairman and CEO of the nonpartisan Liberty and Justice Center (ph), which filed that lawsuit against those earlier tariffs. And she said these new tariffs are not being used the way 301 tariffs are supposed to.

SARA ALBRECHT: It is a negotiating tactic. That is not what tariffs, in a broad sense, are supposed to be. Like, you can do that on a country-by-country basis if they're addressing a specific problem, not just general, hey, we want better trade deals.

KURTZLEBEN: In addition, both she and other trade experts say they think the White House is just proposing these new tariffs as a way to replace the sweeping tariffs the Supreme Court struck down earlier this year.
MARTÍNEZ: Now, we all just found out how unpopular these tariffs were in the midterm elections. So how are these new tariffs landing politically?

KURTZLEBEN: Well, we've heard some real pushback from congressional Democrats. Richard Neal, top House Democrat on the Ways and Means Committee, said in a statement, quote, "Trump is putting everything from family budgets to our national security at risk to keep his tariff scheme in place."

Now, congressional Republicans have been quieter, and this does come a few weeks after they lost dozens of seats in the election, which is widely attributed, in large part, to high prices, and tariffs do cause higher prices.
body_zh: 特朗普政府提议对美国主要贸易伙伴的商品征收新关税特朗普总统提出的新关税已经遭到民主党和一些自由贸易倡导者的抵制。
特朗普总统提出的新关税已经遭到民主党和一些自由贸易倡导者的抵制。
特朗普政府提议对日本、欧盟和中国等美国 14 个最大贸易伙伴的商品征收新关税。有人认为这些新关税是为了对抗其他国家的不公平贸易行为，但目前尚不清楚他们是否真的会这样做。
如需了解更多信息，请听 NPR 白宫记者 Danielle Kurtzleben 的报道。丹妮尔，白宫昨天概述了什么？
丹尼尔·库兹勒本连线：嗯，这是对主要贸易伙伴——你提到的那些，还有韩国和柬埔寨——的商品征收的新关税。中国商品的税率可能高达 40%，越南商品的税率可能高达 35%，其他国家商品的税率可能高达 20% 或 25%。他们还提议对来自巴西的糖和飞机征收额外关税，这将增加美国之前对巴西征收的关税。
马丁内斯：这些计划什么时候才能真正成为现实？
KURTZLEBEN：嗯，它们可能会在几个月内生效。这是美国贸易大使贾米森·格里尔昨天所说的。现在，至于税率是多少，目前还不清楚，因为对于每个国家来说，除了对巴西的额外关税之外，白宫列出了两种税率——提议税率和交易税率。举个例子，对中国的关税可能是20%。这就是成交率。但部分取决于当前讨论的进展情况，中国商品的关税可能高达 40%。
马丁内斯：百分之四十。现在，是的，最高法院撤销了特朗普早些时候的一些关税。那么白宫如何在法律上证明这些新措施的合理性呢？
KURTZLEBEN：嗯，这些是根据简称为“301 条款”的法律实施的，该法律旨在打击其他国家的不公平贸易行为。因此，白宫在这里声称这些其他国家在各种制成品方面存在所谓的结构性产能过剩。政府将这种情况描述为另一个国家的政策导致某种商品生产过剩，从而扭曲该商品的全球市场。因此，根据政府的说法，这些做法可以包括各种各样的内容，例如劳工做法、补贴和税收减免。
现在，美国政府在今年早些时候征收了其他全面的 301 关税，并且有一项诉讼正在审理中，对这些关税提出质疑，关键论点是这些关税的范围比 301 法律要求的范围要广泛得多。
马丁内斯：现在，你提到了一场诉讼。这些新关税是否会面临类似的法律挑战？
KURTZLEBEN：你知道，他们可以。我们会看看会发生什么。但我和萨拉·阿尔布雷希特谈过。她是无党派自由与正义中心（ph）的董事长兼首席执行官，该中心针对先前的关税提起了诉讼。她表示，这些新关税并未按照 301 关税应有的方式使用。
SARA ALBRECHT：这是一种谈判策略。从广义上讲，这并不是关税应有的样子。就像，如果他们解决的是特定问题，而不仅仅是一般性问题，你可以逐个国家这样做，嘿，我们想要更好的贸易协议。
库兹勒本：此外，她和其他贸易专家都表示，他们认为白宫提出这些新关税只是为了取代最高法院今年早些时候驳回的全面关税。
马丁内斯：现在，我们都刚刚发现这些关税在中期选举中是多么不受欢迎。那么这些新关税如何在政治上落地呢？
库兹勒本：嗯，我们听到了国会民主党人的一些真正的反对意见。众议院筹款委员会首席民主党人理查德·尼尔(Richard Neal)在一份声明中表示，“特朗普为了维持他的关税计划，正在将从家庭预算到我们国家安全的一切都置于危险之中。”
现在，国会共和党人变得更加安静，而且这确实发生在他们在选举中失去数十个席位的几周后，人们普遍将这在很大程度上归因于高价格，而关税确实导致了更高的价格。

title_en: Sen. Tim Kaine, D-Va., shares why he opposes Trump's proposed tariffs
title_zh: 弗吉尼亚州民主党参议员蒂姆·凯恩分享了他反对特朗普提议的关税的原因
summary: NPR's A Martinez speaks with Virginia Sen. Tim Kaine about the Democrat's opposition to President Trump's new tariffs.
summary_zh: NPR 的 A Martinez 与弗吉尼亚州参议员 Tim Kaine 谈论了民主党对特朗普总统新关税的反对。
body_en: Sen. Tim Kaine, D-Va., shares why he opposes Trump's proposed tariffs NPR's A Martinez speaks with Virginia Sen. Tim Kaine about the Democrat's opposition to President Trump's new tariffs.
NPR's A Martinez speaks with Virginia Sen. Tim Kaine about the Democrat's opposition to President Trump's new tariffs.

All right. Let's go now to one of the lawmakers who's been trying to fight the president's tariffs in Congress. Democratic Senator Tim Kaine of Virginia backed multiple bills meant to curb or refund the administration's tariffs, including legislation that would constrain the president's ability to impose new tariffs at all.
Senator, happy Thanksgiving. Thanks for joining us on Turkey Day.
TIM KAINE: A, very glad to be with you. And our Turkey Day is going to cost about 6% more than it cost last year...
KAINE: ...Partly because of tariffs. So this is a good topic.
MARTÍNEZ: Well, let's get into that. So the president says the objective is to counter unfair foreign trade practices. What's your view of that rationale?

KAINE: Well, in the big picture, what the president has said is this tariff strategy applied everywhere is going to increase manufacturing jobs in the United States. To the contrary, manufacturing jobs in the United States have declined during President Trump's second term. He also said it would reduce our trade deficit. The trade deficit has increased during President Trump's second term. So neither of the goals that he has have been achieved by his tariff strategy. And one of the things he promised to do - bring prices down - has been dramatically affected in the negative way you saw the inflation numbers yesterday. We're seeing dramatic inflation driven by tariffs in the Iran war. So this is an economic strategy that is a big failure.

MARTÍNEZ: You mentioned manufacturing jobs are not happening in the way that we were told they would happen. But how do you square that with the Steelworkers Union who says that the new tariffs are long overdue?

KAINE: There are particular sectors that like them. I mean, the steel industry likes more steel production in the U.S. But overall, if you look at manufacturing, generally, manufacturing jobs are down. They were up during the Biden administration. They're down during the Trump administration with President Trump saying that the tariffs were going to cause this big manufacturing renaissance.

MARTÍNEZ: So I mentioned your efforts in the Senate to fight the president's tariffs. What is your strongest argument for passing legislation to stop the president from imposing these particular tariffs?

KAINE: So there's a broad argument, and then there's kind of a narrow focused one. So here's the broad one. The Constitution gives tariff power to Congress, not the president. And Congresses of both parties, in my view, have made mistakes over decades in handing off this power, delegating it to the president and allowing the president to impose tariffs on his own. Just to allow one person to impose taxes is not a good idea. And so there are a variety of strategies. I - we - I did work with Senator Paul of Kentucky, and we led the effort against the president's use of the IEEPA statute to impose tariffs. The Supreme Court ultimately struck down...
MARTÍNEZ: International Emergency Economic Powers Act, yeah.

KAINE: That's right, yeah. And the Supreme Court ultimately struck down any imposition of tariffs under that statute. But we're looking at the remaining statutes that Congress has sort of handed the power to the president in one of two ways. You can either repeal those statutes and eliminate any presidential ability to impose tariffs. Or recognizing that presidents sometimes need to move quick - quicker than Congress can - you could allow the president to impose tariffs for a limited period of time, say 60 or 90 days, but those tariffs would expire unless Congress affirmatively validates them and continues them.
So those are some of the legal solutions that are on the table. And with Democratic majorities, I think we have a very good chance of getting some of these bills to President Trump's desk.

MARTÍNEZ: You have 56 U.S. senators in - next year. What's the likelihood that you're going to get enough Republicans that share your view? You mentioned Rand Paul, but you're going to need more if you want to pass legislation that the president can't veto.

KAINE: We will. We - my prediction is we're going to get enough Republican votes in the aftermath of the election, which was really a repudiation of tariffs and the war. We'll get enough Republican votes to put tariff bills on President Trump's desk. Now, here comes the next challenge. If he vetoes those bills, would we have enough to have a two-thirds vote in both Houses to override his veto? That's a - more of an uphill climb. But we're going to test that. We're going to put bills on his desk, dramatically limiting his tariff powers to try to help Americans' pocketbooks. And then we'll say to him, if you veto this bill, you're just going to hurt people. So why don't you just sign it?
body_zh: 弗吉尼亚州民主党参议员蒂姆·凯恩 (Tim Kaine) 分享了他反对特朗普提议的关税的原因 NPR 的马丁内斯 (A Martinez) 与弗吉尼亚州参议员蒂姆·凯恩 (Tim Kaine) 谈论了民主党对特朗普总统新关税的反对。
NPR 的 A Martinez 与弗吉尼亚州参议员 Tim Kaine 谈论了民主党对特朗普总统新关税的反对。
好的。现在让我们来看看一位一直试图在国会反对总统关税的议员。弗吉尼亚州民主党参议员蒂姆·凯恩支持多项旨在遏制或退还政府关税的法案，其中包括限制总统征收新关税能力的立法。
参议员，感恩节快乐。感谢您在火鸡日加入我们。
蒂姆·凯恩：A，很高兴和你在一起。我们的火鸡节费用将比去年增加约 6%...
凯恩：……部分是因为关税。所以这是一个很好的话题。
马丁内斯：好吧，让我们开始吧。因此总统表示，目标是打击不公平的外贸行为。您对此理由有何看法？

凯恩：嗯，从大局来看，总统所说的是，这种在各地实施的关税策略将增加美国的制造业就业机会。相反，在特朗普总统第二任期内，美国制造业就业岗位有所下降。他还表示，这将减少我们的贸易逆差。特朗普总统第二任期内贸易逆差有所增加。因此，他的关税策略并没有实现他的这两个目标。他承诺要做的事情之一——降低物价——已经受到了巨大的负面影响，正如你昨天看到的通胀数据一样。我们看到伊朗战争中的关税导致了剧烈的通货膨胀。所以这是一个巨大失败的经济战略。
马丁内斯：您提到制造业工作并没有像我们被告知的那样发生。但您如何看待钢铁工人工会表示新关税早就应该征收的说法呢？
凯恩：有一些特定的部门喜欢它们。我的意思是，钢铁行业希望美国增加钢铁产量。但总的来说，如果你看看制造业，制造业的就业机会普遍下降。他们在拜登执政期间崛起。在特朗普执政期间，这些数字有所下降，特朗普总统表示，关税将带来制造业的大规模复兴。
马丁内斯：所以我提到了你们在参议院为对抗总统关税所做的努力。您认为通过立法阻止总统征收这些特定关税的最有力论据是什么？
凯恩：所以有一个广泛的争论，然后有一个狭隘的焦点争论。这是广义的。宪法将关税权力赋予国会，而不是总统。在我看来，几十年来，两党国会在将这一权力移交给总统并允许总统自行征收关税方面都犯了错误。仅仅让一个人征税并不是一个好主意。所以有各种各样的策略。我——我们——我确实与肯塔基州参议员保罗合作，我们领导了反对总统利用 IEEPA 法规征收关税的努力。最终最高法院驳回了...
马丁内斯：《国际紧急经济权力法》，是的。
凯恩：没错，是的。最高法院最终否决了根据该法规征收的任何关税。但我们正在研究国会通过以下两种方式之一将权力移交给总统的剩余法规。您可以废除这些法规并消除总统征收关税的任何权力。或者认识到总统有时需要迅速采取行动——比国会更快——你可以允许总统在有限的时间内征收关税，比如 60 或 90 天，但这些关税将到期，除非国会确认并继续实施。
这些是摆在桌面上的一些法律解决方案。由于民主党占多数，我认为我们很有可能将其中一些法案提交给特朗普总统。
马丁内斯：明年将有 56 名美国参议员。你获得足够多的共和党人同意你的观点的可能性有多大？你提到了兰德·保罗，但如果你想通过总统无法否决的立法，你将需要更多。

凯恩：我们会的。我们 - 我的预测是，我们将在选举后获得足够的共和党选票，这实际上是对关税和战争的否定。我们将获得足够的共和党选票，将关税法案放到特朗普总统的办公桌上。现在，下一个挑战来了。如果他否决这些法案，我们是否有足够的票数在参众两院获得三分之二的票数来推翻他的否决？这更像是一次艰难的攀登。但我们要测试一下。我们将把账单放在他的办公桌上，极大地限制他试图帮助美国人改善钱包的关税权力。然后我们会对他说，如果你否决这项法案，你只会伤害人们。那你为什么不直接签字呢？

body_en: Purse found of woman, 24, swept from California beach three weeks ago | California
Se Nah Park was overwhelmed by a wave at the notorious Panther Beach
The purse of a 24-year-old who was swept into the ocean at a notorious California beach three weeks ago was found on Wednesday, as the west coast saw record high king tides.
The Santa Cruz county sheriff’s office confirmed that Se Nah Park’s purse was found by a beachgoer at 4 Mile Beach, south of Panther Beach, where she was swept away into the ocean on 8 November.
According to a GoFundMe started by Park’s friends, Park and five others had gathered around a bonfire beyond the “keyhole” archway at Panther Beach that night.
Four members of the group, including Park, attempted to make their way back through the keyhole when a powerful wave struck, sweeping Park into the ocean.
The three individuals managed to get back up the cliffslide, but tragically, Park did not.
US Coast Guard suspends search for woman swept out to sea in California
Three weeks later, Park’s body has not been located yet, but the discovery of her purse may lead her community closer towards locating her body. .
The coast guard suspended the active search efforts to find Park on 9 November.

“Given the extensive search effort of the surrounding area and environmental conditions, we have suspended active search efforts pending further developments,” Lt Max Holloway, Sector San Francisco search and rescue mission coordinator, said at the time.

“We worked closely with our partner agencies and exhausted all available resources in our attempt to locate Ms Park. Our deepest condolences are with her family and loved ones,” the statement concluded.
In the weeks since, Park’s family and friends have not given up on their search efforts.
Her family and friends continue to “hold on to the hope that Senah can be found and brought home to rest”, her friends shared in a message on GoFundMe.

圣克鲁斯县治安官办公室证实，Se Nah Park 的钱包是一名海滩游客在 Panther 海滩以南的 4 Mile 海滩发现的，她于 11 月 8 日被冲入大海。
据帕克的朋友发起的 GoFundMe 活动称，那天晚上，帕克和其他五人聚集在黑豹海滩“钥匙孔”拱门外的篝火旁。
包括帕克在内的该小组的四名成员试图从钥匙孔返回，这时一股强大的波浪袭来，将帕克卷入大海。

三周后，帕克的尸体尚未找到，但她的钱包的发现可能会让她的社区更接近找到她的尸体。 。
11 月 9 日，海岸警卫队暂停了寻找帕克的积极搜寻工作。
旧金山地区搜救任务协调员马克斯·霍洛威中尉当时表示：“鉴于周边地区的广泛搜索工作和环境条件，我们已暂停积极的搜索工作，等待进一步的进展。”
声明总结道：“我们与合作伙伴机构密切合作，并用尽一切可用资源来寻找朴女士的下落。我们向她的家人和亲人致以最深切的哀悼。”
此后的几周内，帕克的家人和朋友并没有放弃寻找努力。
她的朋友们在 GoFundMe 上的一条消息中分享道，她的家人和朋友仍然“坚持希望能够找到塞纳并带她回家休息”。

David Brooks of The Atlantic and Jonathan Capehart of MS NOW join Nick Schifrin to discuss the week in politics, including President Trump's relationship with Russia's Vladimir Putin, Jensen Huang’s return to Nvidia and sweeping new tariffs on China, Europe and others.

There's been a lot of news packed into this holiday week, ranging from Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia brokered by President Trump to sweeping new tariffs on China, the E.U., and others.
For some perspective on it all, we turn to Brooks and Capehart. That's David Brooks of "The Atlantic" and Jonathan Capehart of MS NOW.

David, let me start with Jensen Huang, reinstated as CEO of Nvidia, an extraordinary announcement before trading hours on Monday morning. President Trump acknowledged he personally pushed for it. What do you make of his involvement?

Well, first, on the whole Jensen Huang thing, we learned -- we taught all of Americans' children a valuable moral lesson, that we care about morals and character and rules and policies, unless we think it's going to hurt the stock price. And then we don't care about that at all.

And so this was a case of pure utilitarianism. We don't value morality. We value money. And that's the lesson we can take from that. And Donald Trump, that's been his life philosophy of his whole life. So at least we give him grades for consistency.

But as for the role he played, Republicans are supposed to stand for the idea that the government does not run the boardroom, that people who run boardrooms or respond to shareholders and all that kind of stuff, they know what they're doing, and it's not the government's role. That idea has been so shredded by Donald Trump over the last decade.
This is only one of dozens of cases where the government is essentially in the role of semi-socialist running private enterprise.

Jonathan, we have seen some of that from President Trump in the first and second term, reaching into corporate decisions, but never perhaps so brazenly as the acknowledgement that the board itself had to reach out to the U.S. government to be reassured that Jensen himself wasn't a national security risk.

And to add to what David said, because David took the words right out of my mouth, government should not be involved in private enterprise. But when it comes to Donald Trump, we also have to keep another thing ever-present in our in our thinking. The president has a personal financial stake in what happens to -- what happens at Nvidia.

When all of this happened, you -- folks went back and looked at his financial disclosure forms. Between January and September of this year, he has sold between $4.4 million and $12 million worth of Nvidia stock. So, with any decision that the president makes, you always have to look, how does it affect his bottom line?

He can -- you would think that the president would say, this is a national security issue. But he's not going down that route. It only seems he invokes national security with any great effect when it comes to things like the ballroom and the arch.

We should say the president basically has argued Nvidia is too big to fail and Jensen was too important to Nvidia, so that he needed to stay. That's the president's argument. He's been consistent on that.

He's also been consistent, David, for decades on tariffs. And this week he brought back tariffs on China, the E.U., Brazil, Taiwan, and others. The president has long argued this is because of unfair trading practices. Is that right?

But the fact is, the tariff policy that Trump enacted, A, raised prices for Americans, B, messed up American farmworkers, C, did not -- did nothing to increase the amount of manufacturing jobs that exist in this country. So it is a complete failure across the board.

Having said that, I'm a little softer on tariffs toward China than other countries like E.U. and others. The Chinese government has made a decision, which I think is a catastrophic decision for them, which is usually, when countries grow from middle class and they want to become First World, or whatever we're going to call it, they move away from manufacturing to services, which modern economies generally are about.

为了了解这一切的一些观点，我们求助于布鲁克斯和卡普哈特。那是《大西洋月刊》的大卫·布鲁克斯和《MS NOW》的乔纳森·卡普哈特。
大卫，让我从黄仁勋开始，他恢复了英伟达首席执行官的职位，这是周一早上交易时间前宣布的一个非同寻常的消息。特朗普总统承认他亲自推动了这一点。你对他的参与有何看法？
嗯，首先，就整个黄仁勋事件而言，我们学到了——我们给所有美国孩子上了宝贵的道德课，我们关心道德、品格、规则和政策，除非我们认为这会损害股价。然后我们就根本不关心这个了。
所以这是一个纯粹功利主义的例子。我们不重视道德。我们看重金钱。这就是我们可以从中吸取的教训。而唐纳德·特朗普，这就是他一生的人生哲学。所以至少我们给他的一致性评分。
但至于他所扮演的角色，共和党人应该坚持这样一种观点：政府不管理董事会，管理董事会或对股东做出回应的人以及诸如此类的人，他们知道自己在做什么，这不是政府的角色。在过去的十年里，这一想法已被唐纳德·特朗普彻底粉碎。
这只是政府本质上扮演半社会主义经营私营企业角色的数十个案例之一。
乔纳森，我们在特朗普总统的第一和第二任期中看到了其中的一些内容，他介入了公司决策，但也许从未像承认董事会本身必须与美国政府接触以确保詹森本人不会构成国家安全风险那样明目张胆。
补充一下大卫的话，因为大卫的话是从我嘴里说出来的，政府不应该参与私营企业。但当谈到唐纳德·特朗普时，我们还必须牢记另一件事。英伟达发生的事情与总统个人的经济利益息息相关。
当这一切发生时，你们——人们回去查看他的财务披露表格。今年 1 月至 9 月期间，他已出售了价值 440 万美元至 1200 万美元的 Nvidia 股票。因此，对于总统做出的任何决定，你总是必须看看它如何影响他的底线？
他可以——你会认为总统会说，这是一个国家安全问题。但他不会走那条路。看来他只有在涉及舞厅和拱门等事情时才会对国家安全产生巨大影响。
我们应该说，总统基本上认为英伟达太大而不能倒，而詹森对英伟达来说太重要了，所以他需要留下来。这是总统的论点。他在这一点上一直保持一致。
大卫，几十年来他在关税问题上也一直保持一致。本周他恢复了对中国、欧盟、巴西、台湾和其他国家的关税。总统长期以来一直认为这是因为不公平的贸易行为。是这样吗？
但事实是，特朗普颁布的关税政策，A，提高了美国人的价格，B，搞乱了美国农场工人，C，没有——没有增加这个国家现有的制造业就业机会。因此，这是一次彻底的失败。
话虽如此，我对中国的关税态度比欧盟等其他国家要温和一些。和其他人。中国政府已经做出了一个决定，我认为这对他们来说是一个灾难性的决定，通常情况下，当国家从中产阶级成长起来并希望成为第一世界，或者无论我们如何称呼它时，他们就会从制造业转向服务业，而现代经济通常都是围绕服务业进行的。

title_en: ACLU seeks court order blocking Trump administration's efforts to unmask ICE critics on social media
title_zh: ACLU 寻求法院命令阻止特朗普政府在社交媒体上揭露 ICE 批评者的努力
summary: Civil rights attorneys claim the Trump administration is abusing the grand jury process in an effort to unmask social media users anonymously criticizing its immigration enforcement tactics
summary_zh: 民权律师声称特朗普政府滥用大陪审团程序，试图揭露社交媒体用户的匿名批评
body_en: Civil rights attorneys claim the Trump administration is abusing the grand jury process in an effort to unmask social media users anonymously criticizing its immigration enforcement tactics

WASHINGTON -- The Trump administration is abusing the grand jury process in an effort to unmask social media users anonymously criticizing its immigration enforcement tactics, civil rights attorneys claim in a federal court filing Friday .

A federal class action, backed by the American Civil Liberties Union, seeks a court order enjoining the Justice Department and Department of Homeland Security from conducting a “bad-faith investigation” that violates the anonymous individuals' First Amendment free speech rights.

The scope of the investigation remains a mystery, but the ACLU says government lawyers have issued dozens of grand jury subpoenas seeking to identify critics and provide their personal information to U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement investigators.

ACLU attorneys sued on behalf of four unnamed social media users, asking the district court in Washington to block subpoenas seeking account information for users of social media companies, including Meta, Bluesky and X, formerly known as Twitter. Chief Judge James Boasberg ordered the ACLU case's unsealing on Wednesday.

Boasberg scheduled a Jan. 6 hearing for arguments on the ACLU’s request for a preliminary injunction against the government. The administration has until Dec. 14 to respond in writing to the ACLU’s allegations.

Spokespeople for DHS and U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro's office in Washington didn't immediately respond to requests for comment. Pirro, Attorney General Todd Blanche and DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin are named as defendants in the ACLU's lawsuit.
ACLU lawyers say Pirro's office has used the term “Investigation 18” to describe efforts to identify and obtain the personal information.
"The investigation," the ACLU says, “is a bad-faith fishing expedition initiated to gather intrusive intelligence and facilitate retaliation against dissenters.”

'The threat is finally real': Judge rips White House 'weaponization'

The ACLU says its lawsuit in Washington is the “first systemic civil challenge, and the first case that will be litigated in public view, to the Trump administration’s abuse of grand jury unmasking subpoenas.”
“The government is weaponizing the grand jury process to retaliate against people for expressing their political views online,” ACLU attorney Laura Moraff said in a statement .

The ACLU argues that the subpoenas to social media platforms are part of a broader pattern of intimidation. DHS has sent hundreds of administrative subpoenas to tech companies in the past year to seek information about online ICE critics, the ACLU says.

The civil rights organization says the Trump administration has shifted to using grand jury subpoenas — a more secretive process — after encountering pushback to the administrative subpoenas from users and tech companies.

The ACLU lawsuit's plaintiffs include a Bluesky user who wrote about an ICE-related shooting in New York by posting: “Burn ICE to the ground. Burn DHS to the ground. Salt the earth.” Another plaintiff is a college student whose posts on X included an expletive directed at DHS, ICE and Trump.

“Defendants’ rampant use of subpoenas to unmask critics of the federal government is occurring against the backdrop of repeated suggestions that Defendants are building a database of dissenters,” ACLU lawyers wrote.
body_zh: 民权律师声称特朗普政府正在滥用大陪审团程序，以揭露社交媒体用户匿名批评其移民执法策略的真相
华盛顿——民权律师周五在联邦法院提交的文件中声称，特朗普政府正在滥用大陪审团程序，试图揭露匿名批评其移民执法策略的社交媒体用户。
美国公民自由联盟支持的联邦集体诉讼寻求法院命令，禁止司法部和国土安全部进行侵犯匿名个人第一修正案言论自由权的“恶意调查”。
调查的范围仍然是个谜，但美国公民自由联盟表示，政府律师已发出数十张大陪审团传票，寻求识别批评者并向美国移民和海关执法局调查人员提供他们的个人信息。
美国公民自由联盟律师代表四名未透露姓名的社交媒体用户提起诉讼，要求华盛顿地区法院阻止向社交媒体公司（包括 Meta、Bluesky 和 ​​X（前身为 Twitter））用户索取账户信息的传票。周三，首席法官詹姆斯·博阿斯伯格下令开启美国公民自由联盟案件。
博阿斯伯格安排于 1 月 6 日举行听证会，就美国公民自由联盟提出的针对政府的初步禁令的请求进行辩论。政府必须在 12 月 14 日之前对 ACLU 的指控做出书面回应。
国土安全部发言人和美国检察官珍妮·皮罗 (Jeanine Pirro) 华盛顿办公室没有立即回应置评请求。皮罗、司法部长托德·布兰奇和国土安全部部长马克韦恩·穆林被列为美国公民自由联盟诉讼的被告。
ACLU 律师表示，皮罗办公室使用了“调查 18”一词来描述识别和获取个人信息的努力。
美国公民自由联盟表示，“这项调查是一次恶意的钓鱼探险，旨在收集侵入性情报并促进对持不同政见者的报复。”

美国公民自由联盟表示，其在华盛顿提起的诉讼是“第一个系统性民事挑战，也是第一个在公众视野中针对特朗普政府滥用大陪审团揭露传票的行为提起诉讼的案件。”
美国公民自由联盟律师劳拉·莫拉夫在一份声明中表示：“政府正在将大陪审团程序武器化，以报复那些在网上表达政治观点的人。”
美国公民自由联盟认为，向社交媒体平台发出传票是更广泛的恐吓模式的一部分。美国公民自由联盟表示，过去一年，国土安全部已向科技公司发出了数百张行政传票，以寻求有关在线 ICE 批评者的信息。
该民权组织表示，在遭到用户和科技公司对行政传票的抵制后，特朗普政府已转向使用大陪审团传票——这是一种更加秘密的程序。
ACLU 诉讼的原告包括一名 Bluesky 用户，他在纽约发生的与 ICE 相关的枪击事件中写道：“将 ICE 烧毁。将 DHS 烧毁。给地球撒盐。”另一名原告是一名大学生，他在 X 上发布的帖子包括针对国土安全部、移民和海关执法局和特朗普的咒骂语。
美国公民自由联盟的律师写道：“被告猖獗地使用传票来揭露对联邦政府的批评者，而这正是在人们一再暗示被告正在建立异议者数据库的背景下发生的。”

title_en: NY Senate leader Andrea Stewart-Cousins, first woman in the role, dies at 76
title_zh: 纽约州参议院领袖安德里亚·斯图尔特-考辛斯 (Andrea Stewart-Cousins) 去世，享年 76 岁，第一位担任该职位的女性
summary: New York state Senate Majority Leader Andrea Stewart-Cousins has died
summary_zh: 纽约州参议院多数党领袖安德里亚·斯图尔特-考辛斯去世
body_en: New York state Senate Majority Leader Andrea Stewart-Cousins has died

NEW YORK -- New York state Senate Majority Leader Andrea Stewart-Cousins, the first woman to lead the chamber, died Friday, her office said. She was 76. Her rise opened doors in a state where top decision-makers had long been dubbed “three men in a room.”

A senator since 2006, Stewart-Cousins had just been reelected by her constituents on Nov. 3, and her fellow Democrats chose mid-month to retain her as their leader. Mike Murphy, a spokesperson for the Senate's Democratic majority, announced her death Friday but didn't give the cause or location.

“She was a groundbreaking leader who shattered one of New York's highest glass ceilings,” he said. Gov. Kathy Hochul, a fellow Democrat, said in a statement that she was heartbroken by the death of a legislator she admired “more than she could have ever known.”
“She never forgot where she came from, who she was fighting for or the doors she could open for those coming behind her,” the governor said.

She had led Senate Democrats since 2012. After her party won control of the chamber, she became majority leader in 2019 — the first woman and first Black woman to hold the post — and promised to “give New Yorkers the progressive leadership they have been demanding.” Her ascension also shook up the state's clubby politics, in which the budget and other key bills were routinely hammered out by the so-called “three men in a room” — the governor and the Senate and Assembly leaders.
“I have not been in the room,” Stewart-Cousins told The Associated Press at the time. “So that will be a difference right there.”

Stewart-Cousins used her role to advance some liberal priorities that were going nowhere when Republicans controlled the Senate, such as legalizing marijuana and strengthening gun control laws. She also led an effort to secure voter approval of a state constitutional amendment that supporters billed as protecting abortion rights .

Stewart-Cousins also prioritized passing voting rights laws and a slate of police accountability measures that gained momentum after the 2020 police killing of George Floyd in Minneapolis. She called it “a moment of reckoning" and commended the advocacy of Valerie Bell and Gwen Carr, whose sons — Sean Bell and Eric Garner — were killed by New York City police.

'The threat is finally real': Judge rips White House 'weaponization'

“Andrea used her authority in the state Senate to help turn what those mothers had fought for into law,” the Rev. Al Sharpton recalled in a statement Friday. Stunned by her death, the civil rights activist noted that the senator was a guest on “PoliticsNation,” his show on MS NOW, just last week.

In a notable moment in 2021, she became the first senior New York Democrat to call for three-term Democratic Gov. Andrew Cuomo to resign amid mounting sexual harassment allegations and a separate controversy over his administration's count of COVID-19 deaths among nursing home residents. Cuomo, who denied the allegations, initially insisted he wouldn't and shouldn't step down, but he ultimately did .
Cuomo said Friday that while they “did not agree on everything,” he was proud of legislation they worked together to pass.
“She stood up for her members and fought for what she believed was right, without hesitation and always with dignity, grace and class,” Cuomo said in a statement.

A resident of Yonkers, a city just north of the New York City border, Stewart-Cousins was a teacher, sales and marketing professional, and Yonkers city official and Westchester County legislator before she was elected to the state Senate in 2006.
Her husband, Thomas Cousins, died in 2007. Survivors include their children, Kevin, Steven and Candice, and her brother, Robert Stewart Jr.
body_zh: 纽约州参议院多数党领袖安德里亚·斯图尔特-考辛斯去世
纽约——纽约州参议院多数党领袖安德里亚·斯图尔特-考辛斯 (Andrea Stewart-Cousins) 办公室表示，她是第一位领导参议院的女性，她于周五去世。她现年 76 岁。她的崛起为这个州的高层决策者长期以来被称为“三个男人同处一室”的局面打开了大门。
斯图尔特-考辛斯自 2006 年起担任参议员，11 月 3 日刚刚被选民连任，她的民主党同僚在月中选择保留她为党魁。参议院民主党多数派发言人迈克·墨菲周五宣布了她的死亡消息，但没有透露死因或地点。
“她是一位开创性的领导人，打破了纽约最高的玻璃天花板之一，”他说。民主党州长凯西·霍赫尔 (Kathy Hochul) 在一份声明中表示，她对一位她敬佩的立法者的去世感到心碎，“比她想象的还要多”。
州长说：“她永远不会忘记她来自哪里，她为谁而战，或者她可以为她身后的人打开一扇门。”
她自 2012 年以来一直领导参议院民主党。在她的政党赢得众议院控制权后，她于 2019 年成为多数党领袖——第一位担任该职位的女性和第一位黑人女性——并承诺“为纽约人提供他们一直要求的进步领导力”。她的上任也震动了该州的俱乐部政治，其中预算和其他关键法案通常是由所谓的“三人同室”——州长、参议院和议会领导人——敲定的。
“我当时不在房间里，”斯图尔特-考辛斯当时告诉美联社。 “所以这就会有所不同。”
斯图尔特-考辛斯利用她的角色推进了一些自由派优先事项，这些事项在共和党控制参议院时毫无进展，例如大麻合法化和加强枪支管制法。她还努力争取选民批准州宪法修正案，支持者称该修正案旨在保护堕胎权。
斯图尔特-考辛斯还优先考虑通过投票权法和一系列警察问责措施，这些措施在 2020 年明尼阿波利斯警察杀害乔治·弗洛伊德后势头强劲。她称这是“清算的时刻”，并赞扬了瓦莱丽·贝尔和格温·卡尔的倡导，他们的儿子肖恩·贝尔和埃里克·加纳被纽约市警察杀害。

感恩节风暴损坏了建筑物，淹没了街道，导致停电
“威胁终于成为现实”：法官驳斥白宫“武器化”
“安德里亚利用她在州参议院的权力，帮助将这些母亲们争取的东西变成了法律，”阿尔·夏普顿牧师在周五的一份声明中回忆道。这位民权活动人士对她的去世感到震惊，他指出，这位参议员上周还是他在 MS NOW 上的节目“PoliticsNation”的嘉宾。
2021 年的一个值得注意的时刻，她成为第一位呼吁三届民主党州长安德鲁·科莫辞职的纽约州资深民主党人，原因是性骚扰指控不断增加，而且其政府对疗养院居民中 COVID-19 死亡人数的统计也存在争议。科莫否认了这些指控，最初坚称他不会也不应该下台，但他最终还是这么做了。
科莫周五表示，虽然他们“并未在所有问题上达成一致”，但他对他们共同努力通过的立法感到自豪。
科莫在一份声明中说：“她毫不犹豫地为她的成员挺身而出，为她认为正确的事情而奋斗，始终带着尊严、优雅和优雅。”
斯图尔特-考辛斯是纽约市边境以北城市扬克斯的居民，在 2006 年当选为州参议员之前，她曾是一名教师、销售和营销专业人士、扬克斯市官员和威彻斯特县议员。
她的丈夫 Thomas Cousins 于 2007 年去世。幸存者包括他们的孩子 Kevin、Steven 和 Candice，以及她的兄弟 Robert Stewart Jr。

title_en: Thousands still without power after storms that snarled Thanksgiving travel
title_zh: 暴风雨扰乱了感恩节旅行，数千人仍然断电
summary: Heavy rains and high winds downed trees and power lines and led to water rescues from New York to Virginia Skies cleared along the US eastern seaboard on Friday, and power was being restored to hundreds of thousands of customers whose Thanksgiving plans were d
summary_zh: 大雨和大风吹倒了树木和电线，导致从纽约到弗吉尼亚州的水上救援，美国东部沿海地区天空晴朗
body_en: Heavy rains and high winds downed trees and power lines and led to water rescues from New York to Virginia

Skies cleared along the US eastern seaboard on Friday, and power was being restored to hundreds of thousands of customers whose Thanksgiving plans were disrupted by heavy rains and high winds that swept over the region a day earlier.
The storms snarled travel, downed trees and power lines and led to water rescues from New York to Virginia. At its peak, nearly a million customers were without power .

The storms prompted the first-ever postponement of the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day parade in New York City, as well as the delay or cancellation of thousands of flights. In New Jersey widespread flooding reached levels not seen since 2012, after Hurricane Sandy.
By Friday morning, conditions had significantly improved, though hundreds of thousands remained without power and air travel was still affected by significant delays.
On Friday afternoon Poweroutage.us reported 400,577 customers were still without power, including 98,597 in Pennsylvania, 63,658 in Missouri and 60,297 in New Jersey.

Flightaware said delays within, into, or out of the US on Friday stood at 2,489, and cancellations at 144. On Thursday, more than 2,200 flights to or from US destinations had been delayed and more than 400 had been cancelled.
“The bulk of the storm impacts are behind us, but tidal flooding will continue today,” the National Weather Service said early Friday.

Parts of the midwest and the south were dealing with unusual snowfalls for the time of year, with St Louis, Missouri, getting 7.3in, and snow reported in Alabama and Tennessee. An ice arena in Wentzville, Missouri, was empty when the roof caved in at about 3am, according to the city.

“The south and south-east US will start with very cold morning temperatures today and Saturday as lows drop into the upper 20s and the middle 30s,” the National Weather Service said. “Freeze headlines are in effect for portions of the deep south. High temperatures Saturday will begin to moderate into the 60s.”

In New York City, authorities were rushing to clean up the damage the storm left in its wake. Several people had to be rescued from their cars amid flooding, said Zohran Mamdani, and similar rescues were reported in other coastal communities.

Strong winds and flooding disrupted train lines, toppled trees and caused power outages on Thanksgiving night, New York City emergency management officials said. Several scaffolding structures collapsed in the wind, but no injuries were reported.
New York City police said they had recovered a body of man along the Staten Island shoreline. It was not yet clear if the death was storm-related.
The storms also flooded areas from North Carolina through to New Jersey as high tide rolled in. Roads were closed, and emergency workers were rescuing people from cars stranded in water.
Downtown merchants in Avalon, New Jersey , scrambled to pump out saltwater on Friday after Thanksgiving brought some of the most significant tides in the seaside community’s history.

Cheryl McKenna of Ocean City, New Jersey, said water flooded her garage and surrounded her property, keeping her family inside for six hours on the holiday. She said flooding had become more frequent since Superstorm Sandy in 2012.

“Our family’s been here for 36 years,” McKenna said. “But honestly, we’re thinking is this the right place for us to be? We’re now retired, and we want to stay down here, but how often can we continue to do this?”
Donald Trump signed a disaster declaration on Thursday for Florida in response to earlier flooding that damaged hundreds of homes and required water rescues.

The US president had approved funding earlier this week, but gathered local officials on Thanksgiving to talk about it in a small signing ceremony at his home in West Palm Beach. “Since October it has been raining continuously,” the president said. “It’s the craziest thing. It stopped now.”
body_zh: 大雨和大风吹倒了树木和电线，导致从纽约到弗吉尼亚州的水上救援
周五，美国东海岸天空放晴，数十万客户的供电正在恢复，他们的感恩节计划因前一天席卷该地区的大雨和大风而中断。
暴风雨扰乱了交通，摧毁了树木和电线，并导致从纽约到弗吉尼亚州的水上救援。最高峰时，有近百万客户断电。
风暴导致纽约市梅西百货感恩节游行首次推迟，并导致数千架航班延误或取消。新泽西州的大范围洪水达到了 2012 年飓风桑迪以来的最高水平。
到周五早上，情况已显着改善，但仍有数十万人断电，航空旅行仍受到严重延误的影响。
周五下午，Poweroutage.us 报告称，仍有 400,577 名客户断电，其中宾夕法尼亚州 98,597 名，密苏里州 63,658 名，新泽西州 60,297 名。
Flightaware 表示，周五，美国境内、进出美国的航班延误 2,489 架次，取消 144 架次。周四，超过 2,200 架往返美国目的地的航班延误，超过 400 架航班取消。
国家气象局周五早些时候表示：“大部分风暴影响已经过去，但潮汐洪水今天仍将继续。”
中西部和南部的部分地区正在经历一年中不同寻常的降雪，密苏里州圣路易斯的降雪量为 7.3 英寸，阿拉巴马州和田纳西州也有降雪报告。据密苏里州温茨维尔市称，凌晨 3 点左右，当屋顶塌陷时，一座冰场空无一人。
美国国家气象局表示：“今天和周六，美国南部和东南部早晨气温将非常寒冷，最低气温将降至 20 多度到 30 多度。” “南方腹地部分地区出现了冰冻头条新闻。周六的高温将开始降至 60 多度。”
在纽约市，当局正在紧急清理风暴造成的破坏。佐赫兰·马姆达尼 (Zohran Mamdani) 表示，在洪水中，有几个人不得不从车里被救出来，其他沿海社区也有类似的救援行动。
纽约市应急管理官员表示，感恩节晚上，强风和洪水扰乱了火车线路，导致树木倒塌，并导致停电。多个脚手架结构在风中倒塌，但没有人员伤亡的报告。
纽约市警方表示，他们在史泰登岛海岸线发现了一具男子尸体。目前尚不清楚死亡是否与风暴有关。
随着涨潮的到来，风暴还淹没了从北卡罗来纳州到新泽西州的地区。道路被封闭，紧急救援人员正在从被困水中的汽车中救出人们。
感恩节带来了沿海社区历史上最严重的潮汐后，周五，新泽西州阿瓦隆市中心的商人争先恐后地抽出盐水。
新泽西州大洋城的谢丽尔·麦肯纳 (Cheryl McKenna) 表示，水淹没了她的车库并包围了她的财产，导致她的家人在假期里呆了六个小时。她说，自 2012 年超级风暴桑迪以来，洪水变得更加频繁。
“我们一家人在这里已经 36 年了，”麦肯纳说。 “但说实话，我们在想这对我们来说是合适的地方吗？我们现在退休了，我们想留在这里，但我们多久可以继续这样做呢？”
唐纳德·特朗普周四签署了佛罗里达州灾难声明，以应对早些时候造成数百座房屋受损并需要水上救援的洪水。
美国总统本周早些时候批准了这笔资金，但感恩节那天聚集了当地官员，在他位于西棕榈滩的家中举行的小型签字仪式上讨论了这一问题。 “自十月以来，一直在下雨，”总统说。 “这是最疯狂的事情。现在停止了。”

title_en: Jared Kushner’s 70-minute interview reveals naive bias in handling of Putin’s aggression
title_zh: 贾里德·库什纳 (Jared Kushner) 70 分钟的采访揭示了处理普京侵略行为时的天真偏见

summary_zh: 特朗普的女婿兼高级谈判代表在 70 分钟的采访中将俄罗斯入侵乌克兰描述为需要解决的误会
body_en: Trump’s son-in-law and senior negotiator paints Russian invasion of Ukraine as a misunderstanding to be resolved

In the space of a 70-minute interview, Jared Kushner – Donald Trump’s son-in-law and a prominent US negotiator in Russia, Gaza and Iran – probably did more to reveal why the world is mired in entrenched conflicts than a thousand geopolitical tomes or seminars.

During the conversation this week with Mathias Döpfner, the chief executive of the Axel Springer media publisher, Kushner gave a rare insight into his diplomatic technique, offering a string of homilies that veered close to banalities: “You have nothing until you have something”, “diplomacy is like untying knots on a fishing line for his son”, and “you play the ball from where it lands”.

There were also many happy admissions of historical ignorance. Since taking on the Ukraine brief a year ago, Kushner said, he had to learn “the algorithm of Europe and how complicated that is”, and he had to get abreast of “the local issues with Ukraine”.

As a businessman he brought a special expertise, he claimed. “Look at what’s happening in the Middle East with sanctions, with Russia , with Iran. I think that you have to understand economics in order to understand geopolitics because the two go together very, very closely,” he said.
But the main revelation was how much he believes the Ukraine conflict is not a case of an aggressor and a victim – but is simply a series of misunderstandings and miscommunication.

Indeed, he treated Vladimir Putin as if he were a masterful corporate executive quite willing to close the deal if he were only given the right economic incentives – instead of a man ready to sacrifice hundreds of thousands of Russians to reclaim part of a historical empire .

In the process, Kushner revealed – often inadvertently – that he had largely bought into the Russian narrative of a string of postwar missteps by Europe and the US coming to a head in Nato’s expansion eastwards after 9/11.

That, in turn, has led him to adopt Moscow’s central demand to reshape the European security order to allow Russia, without opprobrium, to retain land it has gained by force. Shining through his answers was a naive bias towards the aggressor, presented as a mediator’s desire to understand both parties.

Praise veering on awe for the Russian leader flowed. “Putin – people can like what he has done, they can not like what he has done – [but] he is a grand master of politics. He is a historic figure,” he said. Any sense that Putin may have blundered escaped him.

As to the rights and wrongs of invading another country, Kushner was blasé. “After all, most lines in Europe have changed over time and they are decided through war or peace, or concessions. It’s not about fairness or who is right or wrong. It’s about ending the killing,” he said.

He understood, too, why Putin could not offer a ceasefire: “He has very little confidence that if he stops the war, that he [will] be able to get to a postwar settlement that leads to not having a future war.”
To stop the killing, the killing has to go on.
What is more, Kushner was struck by the Russian leader’s self-control. “So far Putin has shown restraint and he has agreed not to use nuclear weapons and he has reassured us that is his intention.”

Kushner denied Trump had put any pressure on Volodymyr Zelenskyy, defying his interviewer to provide evidence – at which point Döpfner recited a list of examples, including only last month when the US president suggested that Ukraine should get a new leader .

Trump was “a strong counter-puncher”, argued Kushner, implying that Zelenskyy had thrown the first punch in a conflict that began with a Russian invasion. Relations with Ukraine were cooperative, he said before pointedly saying Kyiv needed things from the US, without which “Ukraine will not be safe in the future”.

After noting that “the territorial issue is now a little bit of a deadlock”, his strategic insight was that if a future security architecture for Europe could be agreed, the answer to the land question in Donbas would eventually follow.
In essence, he proposed a revival of the Russia-Nato council, one of the bodies eviscerated by Putin’s war.

He also envisioned Ukraine inside the European Union with security guarantees akin to those offered by Nato’s article five. Though it was impossible at this stage to give “more specificity” about these guarantees in the detailed way Ukraine sought, he admitted.
body_zh: 特朗普的女婿兼高级谈判代表将俄罗斯入侵乌克兰视为需要解决的误会
在长达 70 分钟的采访中，贾里德·库什纳（Jared Kushner）——唐纳德·特朗普的女婿、美国在俄罗斯、加沙和伊朗的著名谈判代表——可能比上千本地缘政治书籍或研讨会更能揭示世界为何陷入根深蒂固的冲突。
在本周与阿克塞尔·施普林格媒体出版商首席执行官马蒂亚斯·多普夫纳的谈话中，库什纳对自己的外交技巧进行了罕见的洞察，并提出了一系列近乎平庸的说教：“除非你有所收获，否则你将一无所有”、“外交就像为他儿子解开钓鱼线上的结”以及“你从球落地的地方打球”。
还有许多人高兴地承认对历史的无知。库什纳说，自从一年前接受乌克兰简报以来，他必须学习“欧洲的算法以及它有多复杂”，他必须了解“乌克兰的当地问题”。
他声称，作为一名商人，他带来了特殊的专业知识。 “看看中东发生的事情，包括俄罗斯、伊朗的制裁。我认为，你必须了解经济学才能了解地缘政治，因为这两者非常非常密切地结合在一起，”他说。
但主要的启示是，他多么相信乌克兰冲突不是侵略者和受害者的问题，而只是一系列误解和沟通不畅的问题。
事实上，他对待弗拉基米尔·普京的态度就好像他是一位精明的企业高管，只要给予适当的经济激励，他就愿意完成交易——而不是一个准备牺牲数十万俄罗斯人来夺回历史帝国一部分的人。
在此过程中，库什纳经常无意间透露，他在很大程度上接受了俄罗斯关于欧洲和美国战后一系列失误的叙述，这些失误在9/11之后北约向东扩张的过程中达到了顶峰。
这反过来又导致他采纳莫斯科的核心要求，重塑欧洲安全秩序，让俄罗斯不受谴责地保留其通过武力获得的土地。从他的回答中可以看出，他对攻击者有一种天真的偏见，表现为调解人想要了解双方的愿望。
人们对这位俄罗斯领导人的赞誉转而敬畏。 “普京——人们可以喜欢他所做的事情，也可以不喜欢他所做的事情——[但]他是一位伟大的政治大师。他是一位历史人物，”他说。他完全没有意识到普京可能犯了错误。
至于入侵另一个国家的对错，库什纳对此漠不关心。 “毕竟，欧洲的大多数路线都随着时间的推移而发生了变化，它们是通过战争或和平或让步来决定的。这与公平或谁对谁错无关。这是关于结束杀戮，”他说。
他也理解普京为何不能提出停火：“他对如果停止战争就能够达成战后解决方案，从而避免未来发生战争，几乎没有信心。”
为了阻止杀戮，杀戮必须继续下去。
更重要的是，库什纳对这位俄罗斯领导人的自制力感到震惊。 “到目前为止，普京表现出了克制，他同意不使用核武器，他向我们保证这是他的意图。”
库什纳否认特朗普对弗拉基米尔·泽连斯基施加了任何压力，不顾采访者提供证据——此时德普夫纳列举了一系列例子，包括上个月美国总统建议乌克兰应该找到一位新领导人。
库什纳认为，特朗普是“强有力的反击者”，这意味着泽连斯基在以俄罗斯入侵为起点的冲突中打出了第一拳。他表示，与乌克兰的关系是合作性的，然后尖锐地表示基辅需要美国的东西，没有美国“乌克兰未来将不安全”。
在指出“领土问题现在有点陷入僵局”后，他的战略洞察力是，如果能够就欧洲未来的安全架构达成一致，顿巴斯土地问题的答案最终就会随之而来。
从本质上讲，他提议复兴俄罗斯-北约理事会，这是被普京战争摧毁的机构之一。
他还设想乌克兰在欧盟内部获得类似于北约第五条所提供的安全保障。他承认，尽管现阶段不可能按照乌克兰寻求的详细方式对这些保证进行“更具体”的说明。
