summary_zh: 两党的《美国负担能力和就业法案》已在参议院获得通过，目前正在众议院进行辩论 行业支持的“许可法案”批准
body_en: US Senate ‘permitting bill’ threatens clean water protections to speed up energy projects | US politics
The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act passed the Senate and is now being debated in the House

An industry-backed “permitting bill” approved by the US Senate would gut key clean water protections with changes that would do little to speed up the development of major energy projects, advocates warn.

The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026 (Baaja) passed the Senate 62-33 and is now being debated in the House. The Baaja is a “permitting reform” bill that aims to reduce the time it takes federal agencies to approve major energy and infrastructure projects, like power lines, fossil fuel pipelines, natural gas plants and datacenters .

But the legislation also includes provisions that would make it more difficult for states to put in place protections against water pollution, double the amount of time between automatic reviews of water pollution permits, and reduce transparency around the types and levels of water pollution.

More than 50 groups in communities affected by Pfas “forever chemical” water pollution have come out against the bill , warning that they would suffer further if the legislation is approved because it would weaken some of the few mechanisms in US law that regulate the chemicals’ discharge. The law would “put us in more danger”, said Emily Donovan, co-founder of the Clean Cape Fear advocacy group in Wilmington, North Carolina, where drinking, surface and ground water is polluted by discharge from a nearby Pfas factory .
“We already see how hard it is for the [Environmental Protection Agency (EPA)] to [regulate] Pfas ,” Donovan said. “What frustrates us is we don’t need to make it harder.”

Baaja has drawn wide industry support , including among trade groups such as the American Chemistry Council and American Petroleum Institute . It is opposed by virtually every major US environmental group because it would eliminate some foundational environmental protections.

The bill’s supporters say the cost is worth it because it will allow energy projects to be built faster, and hasten the transition to clean energy. Opponents say industry is using the need to transition to clean energy as cover to ram through a range of unnecessary changes to water laws that do nothing to improve energy permitting.

“BAAJA is a handout to the oil and gas industry, while doing very little to solve the permitting problems being used to justify those changes,” the Clean Water Action advocacy group, which is lobbying against the law, said in a statement. “Congress is trading away protections for states, tribes, wetlands and streams even though those protections are largely unrelated to the years-long delays at the center of the permitting debate.”

Among other changes, the bill would allow industry to sue to undo the EPA’s guidance for states on water pollution discharge. The EPA currently develops criteria that states use to limit discharge into waterways. The agency does this without issuing a formal rule, and the criteria cannot easily be challenged in court.

The Baaja would require a formal rule-making process, which would slow the clean water criteria issuance by several years, and open it to lawsuits. The criteria are used by states to develop limits on Pfas water pollution, and the change would shift more responsibility on to states that are largely underresourced and unable to meet the challenge, Donovan said.

Another provision would change the EPA’s mandatory review of water pollution permits from five years to 10 years. The EPA uses this review mechanism to require polluters to track their Pfas and other water pollution.

Donovan pointed to the Pfas pollution in North Carolina to highlight how the provision would prolong the public’s exposure to dangerous chemicals. North Carolina regulators in 2019 put in place a health advisory limit of 140 parts per tn (ppt) for GenX, one of the main Pfas compounds polluting the state’s waterways. By 2022, the EPA established a health advisory of 10 ppt.

Advocates fear that the extended review period for pollution permits from five to 10 years would create a scenario in which a company issued a water permit in 2020 may continue to pollute at higher levels for much longer.

“Imagine not being able to make a change for 10 years despite that the science is showing that a chemical is more toxic than originally thought – that’s what terrifies and frustrates us,” Donovan said. The transition to clean energy does not need to sacrifice clean water, she added.
“We can get clean energy without having to cause cancer,” Donovan said.
body_zh: 美国参议院“许可法案”威胁清洁水保护以加速能源项目美国政治
两党共同通过的《美国负担能力和就业法案》已在参议院获得通过，目前正在众议院进行辩论
支持者警告说，美国参议院批准的一项得到行业支持的“许可法案”将破坏关键的清洁水保护，其变化对加快重大能源项目的发展几乎无济于事。
两党共同制定的 2026 年美国负担能力和就业法案 (Baaja) 在参议院以 62 比 33 获得通过，目前正在众议院进行辩论。 Baaja 是一项“许可改革”法案，旨在减少联邦机构批准重大能源和基础设施项目（如输电线、化石燃料管道、天然气厂和数据中心）所需的时间。
但该立法还包括一些条款，这些条款将使各州更难实施水污染保护措施，使水污染许可证自动审查之间的时间加倍，并降低水污染类型和水平的透明度。
受 Pfas“永久化学”水污染影响的社区中的 50 多个团体已站出来反对该法案，并警告说，如果该法案获得批准，他们将遭受进一步的损失，因为这将削弱美国法律中少数几个管理化学品排放的机制。北卡罗来纳州威尔明顿清洁开普恐惧倡导组织的联合创始人艾米丽·多诺万表示，这项法律将“让我们陷入更大的危险”，那里的饮用水、地表水和地下水均因附近一家 Pfas 工厂的排放而受到污染。
“我们已经看到 [环境保护局 (EPA)] [监管] Pfa 有多么困难，”多诺万说。 “令我们沮丧的是我们不需要让事情变得更难。”
Baaja 得到了广泛的行业支持，包括美国化学理事会和美国石油协会等贸易团体的支持。它几乎遭到美国所有主要环保组织的反对，因为它将消除一些基本的环境保护措施。
该法案的支持者表示，这笔成本是值得的，因为它将使能源项目建设更快，并加速向清洁能源的过渡。反对者表示，工业界正在利用向清洁能源过渡的需要作为掩护，强行对水法进行一系列不必要的修改，而这些修改对改善能源许可毫无帮助。
正在游说反对这项法律的清洁水行动倡导组织在一份声明中表示，“BAAJA 是对石油和天然气行业的一份施舍，但几乎没有解决用于证明这些变化合理性的许可问题。” “国会正在放弃对州、部落、湿地和溪流的保护，尽管这些保护在很大程度上与许可辩论中心长达数年的拖延无关。”
除其他变化外，该法案将允许工业界提起诉讼，以撤销美国环保局对各州水污染排放的指导。美国环保署目前制定了各州用于限制向水道排放的标准。该机构在没有发布正式规则的情况下做到了这一点，而且这些标准不能轻易在法庭上受到质疑。
Baaja 将需要一个正式的规则制定程序，这将使清洁水标准的发布速度推迟数年，并导致诉讼。多诺万说，各州使用这些标准来制定对 Pfas 水污染的限制，这一变化将把更多的责任转移到资源严重不足且无法应对挑战的各州身上。
另一项规定将把 EPA 对水污染许可证的强制审查从五年改为 10 年。 EPA 使用这种审查机制要求污染者追踪其 Pfa 和其他水污染。
多诺万指出北卡罗来纳州的 Pfas 污染，强调该规定将如何延长公众接触危险化学品的时间。北卡罗来纳州监管机构于 2019 年对 GenX 制定了每吨 140 份 (ppt) 的健康建议限值，GenX 是污染该州水道的主要 Pfas 化合物之一。到 2022 年，EPA 制定了 10 ppt 的健康建议。
支持者担心，将排污许可证的审查期从 5 年延长至 10 年将造成这样一种情况：2020 年颁发取水许可证的公司可能会在更长的时间内继续以更高的水平进行污染。
“想象一下，尽管科学表明某种化学物质的毒性比最初想象的要大，但 10 年内都无法做出改变，这就是让我们感到恐惧和沮丧的原因，”多诺万说。她补充说，向清洁能源的过渡不需要牺牲清洁水。
“我们可以获得清洁能源，而不会导致癌症，”多诺万说。

title_en: Power being slowly restored as heavy Thanksgiving storm eases
title_zh: 随着感恩节风暴的减弱，电力正在慢慢恢复
summary: Heavy rain over flooded East Coast communities began easing Friday, and power was slowly restored to hundreds of thousands of customers.
summary_zh: 周五，被洪水淹没的东海岸社区的大雨开始缓解，数十万用户的供电也慢慢恢复。
body_en: Power being slowly restored as heavy Thanksgiving storm eases, but flood risk remains - CBS News

Heavy rain over flooded East Coast communities began easing Friday, and power was slowly restored to hundreds of thousands of customers as some places stayed on guard for high-tide flooding following a round of holiday storms .

The storms snarled travel and downed trees and power lines. The heavy weather led to water rescues from New York to Virginia. In New York City , preparations were underway to hold Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade on Saturday after an unprecedented postponement because of rain and high winds.

Elsewhere, wet snow fell as far south as the Tennessee Valley and freezing rain moved across northern New England. Cold rain was reported in parts of the Midwest, including the Ohio Valley and the lower Great Lakes.
Another storm system in the Northwest brought rain along coastal Oregon. More snow was forecast in the Cascade Range and in mountain passes in Montana and Wyoming.
There were just under 3,700 flights in the U.S. delayed as of Friday night, with another 162 canceled, according to the flight tracking service FlightAware .
The number of power outages, which peaked Thursday at more than 900,000 customers, fell to just under 300,000 by Friday night, according to utility tracker PowerOutage.us.
Bad weather in the East is taking its time to go

Conditions were expected to improve Friday across the entire eastern U.S., "but this huge system will take some time to weaken," the National Weather Service said on its website. Coastal flood warnings were posted from New Jersey to Virginia.
"A lot of standing water, tree branches, siding ripped off of houses and buildings," homeowner Chris Rizzo told CBS New York.

In Hampton, Virginia, the storm toppled a beloved landmark at Grandview Beach: a weathered, leafless tree known as the "Grieving Tree" or the "Shell Tree." Visitors regularly decorated its branches with seashells, and it became a popular subject for photographers.
After surviving many storms, the tree "may have finally met its match," local meteorologist Ricky Matthews wrote on Facebook, sharing a photograph.
Roofs in Ocean City and Rockville collapsed. In Norfolk, Virginia, crews rescued 39 people and two dogs, City Councilman Tommy Smigiel posted.

In Baltimore , the storm brought a record 3.04 inches of rain to BWI Thurgood Marshall Airport on Thursday, while high tide in Annapolis reached 4.48 feet that night, a level officials said was among the 10 highest on record.
Part of a fishing pier collapsed in Virginia Beach, Virginia, closing a 3-mile section of beach, including the boardwalk, "due to dangerous conditions," the city said.

Downtown merchants in Avalon, New Jersey, scrambled to pump out saltwater Friday after Thanksgiving brought some of the most significant tides in the seaside community's history. More than 1,100 people participated in a charity run, and Santa Claus was scheduled to arrive on a fire truck by evening to light the Christmas tree.
Conditions were a "million times better than they were 24 hours ago," borough business administrator Scott Wahl said.

Cheryl McKenna of Ocean City, New Jersey, said water flooded her garage and surrounded her property, keeping her family inside for six hours on the holiday. She said flooding has become more frequent since Superstorm Sandy in 2012.

"Our family has been here for 36 years," McKenna said. "But honestly, we're thinking, is this the right place for us to be? We're now retired, and we want to stay down here, but how often can we continue to do this."

Another round of rain and strong winds are expected to hit the East Coast by Sunday evening, potentially disrupting the Monday morning commute. Up to 2 inches of rain and wind gusts of 65 mph are possible in some areas, according to CBS News meteorologist Nikki Nolan.
body_zh: 随着感恩节风暴的缓解，电力正在慢慢恢复，但洪水风险仍然存在 - 哥伦比亚广播公司新闻
周五，被洪水淹没的东海岸社区的大雨开始缓解，数十万用户的供电慢慢恢复，一些地方在一轮假日风暴后仍保持警惕，以防洪水泛滥。
暴风雨扰乱了交通，摧毁了树木和电线。恶劣的天气导致从纽约到弗吉尼亚州的水上救援。在纽约市，梅西百货感恩节大游行因降雨和大风而史无前例地推迟，周六的感恩节大游行的准备工作正在进行中。
在其他地方，湿雪一直向南降落到田纳西河谷，冻雨横扫新英格兰北部。据报道，中西部部分地区出现冷雨，包括俄亥俄河谷和五大湖下游。
西北地区的另一个风暴系统给俄勒冈州沿海地区带来了降雨。预计喀斯喀特山脉以及蒙大拿州和怀俄明州的山口将有更多降雪。
根据航班跟踪服务 FlightAware 的数据，截至周五晚上，美国有近 3,700 架航班延误，另有 162 架航班取消。
据公用事业跟踪机构 PowerOutage.us 称，周四停电数量达到峰值，超过 90 万客户，到周五晚上已降至不到 30 万。
东部地区的恶劣天气正在慢慢消失
美国国家气象局在其网站上表示，预计周五整个美国东部的情况将有所改善，“但这个巨大的系统需要一段时间才能减弱”。从新泽西州到弗吉尼亚州都发布了沿海洪水警告。
房主克里斯·里佐（Chris Rizzo）告诉纽约哥伦比亚广播公司（CBS New York）：“大量积水、树枝、房屋和建筑物的壁板被扯掉。”
在弗吉尼亚州汉普顿，风暴摧毁了格兰德维尤海滩上一棵受人喜爱的地标：一棵饱经风霜、光秃秃的树，被称为“悲伤树”或“贝壳树”。游客经常用贝壳装饰它的树枝，它成为摄影师的热门拍摄对象。
当地气象学家瑞奇·马修斯在脸书上分享了一张照片，在经历了多次风暴后，这棵树“可能终于遇到了对手”。
大洋城和罗克维尔的屋顶倒塌。市议员汤米·斯米吉尔 (Tommy Smigiel) 表示，在弗吉尼亚州诺福克，救援人员救出了 39 人和两只狗。
周四，巴尔的摩的暴风雨给 BWI 瑟古德马歇尔机场带来了创纪录的 3.04 英寸降雨量，安纳波利斯当晚的高潮达到了 4.48 英尺，一级官员称这是有记录以来的 10 个最高潮位之一。
弗吉尼亚州弗吉尼亚海滩称，“由于情况危险”，一个钓鱼码头的一部分倒塌，关闭了包括木板路在内的 3 英里长的海滩区域。
感恩节带来了沿海社区历史上最严重的潮汐后，周五，新泽西州阿瓦隆市中心的商人争先恐后地抽出盐水。超过 1,100 人参加了慈善跑，圣诞老人计划于晚上乘坐消防车抵达并点燃圣诞树。
该区商业管理员斯科特·瓦尔 (Scott Wahl) 表示，情况“比 24 小时前好一百万倍”。
新泽西州大洋城的谢丽尔·麦肯纳 (Cheryl McKenna) 表示，水淹没了她的车库并包围了她的财产，导致她的家人在假期里呆了六个小时。她说，自 2012 年超级风暴桑迪以来，洪水变得更加频繁。
“我们一家人在这里已经 36 年了，”麦肯纳说。 “但说实话，我们在想，这对我们来说是合适的地方吗？我们现在退休了，我们想留在这里，但我们能继续这样做多久呢？”
预计到周日晚上，另一轮降雨和强风将袭击东海岸，可能会扰乱周一早上的通勤。据 CBS 新闻气象学家 Nikki Nolan 称，部分地区可能会出现高达 2 英寸的降雨和时速 65 英里的阵风。

title_en: Trump calls the pre-election GDP figures 'fake' and demands an investigation of Commerce Department
title_zh: 特朗普称选前GDP数据“虚假”并要求商务部进行调查
summary: President Donald Trump is suggesting without evidence a conspiracy within the government to report upwardly revised economic growth figures after the midterm elections that were disastrous for Republicans
summary_zh: 唐纳德·特朗普总统在没有证据的情况下暗示政府内部存在阴谋，在经济增长数据公布后上调了经济增长数据。
body_en: President Donald Trump is suggesting without evidence a conspiracy within the government to report upwardly revised economic growth figures after the midterm elections that were disastrous for Republicans

WEST PALM BEACH, Fla. -- President Donald Trump on Thursday accused his Commerce Department of purposely issuing incorrect economic growth figures before the midterm elections, and said he wants to launch an investigation.

Trump has repeatedly sought to undermine trust in economic data that fails to match his claims of a historic boom, a pattern that threatens the credibility of figures needed by businesses, financial markets and consumers when making investments.

His latest complaint concerns data issued by the Commerce Department on Wednesday that revised gross domestic product in the third quarter to 4.3% on an annual basis, up from a prior estimate of 3.4%.

The department’s Bureau of Economic Analysis routinely updates its economic data to improve their accuracy. GDP figures, monthly jobs reports and other data are regularly revised. Those updates occur on a pre-scheduled basis without regard to the political calendar.

But the president claimed on social media that it was a “massive, and purposeful, error” and linked it to the poor performance for Republicans in the Nov. 3 midterm elections that gave Democrats control of both houses of Congress.

“It was just revealed that the REAL Numbers on the Economy, published before the Election, were FAKE, and a correction was issued yesterday by the people in the Government Agency that does these numbers,” Trump posted. “Why wasn't the correct number issued before the Election? I am asking for an immediate investigation of this situation.”
Federal officials say 'zero' airborne lead detected after Iowa munitions blast
Thanksgiving storm damages buildings, floods streets, causes power outages
'The threat is finally real': Judge rips White House 'weaponization'
The Commerce Department did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The government is largely closed on Thursday for the Thanksgiving holiday.

It’s the latest instance of Trump questioning the integrity of economic data he feels is unfavorable to him without providing evidence that revisions are politically motivated. In August 2025, Trump fired the head of the Bureau of Labor Statistics after a decidedly weak jobs report. That report said only 73,000 jobs were added in July 2025 and showed that 258,000 fewer jobs were added in May and June than previously reported.
Trump called that jobs report “phony” and “rigged.”

Trump has claimed that he deserves credit for powering stronger economic growth, but voters do not share the president's belief that the economy is strong. In the midterms, 76% described economic conditions as “not so good” or “poor,” according to the AP Voter Poll, an extensive survey of the electorate. About two-thirds of voters said Trump’s own policies had fueled inflation.

The president in his social media post ignored that the same federal agency on Wednesday also reported that a key measure of inflation — the personal consumption expenditures price index — accelerated to an annual pace of 3.8% in October.
body_zh: 唐纳德·特朗普总统在没有证据的情况下暗示政府内部存在阴谋，在中期选举后上调经济增长数据，这对共和党来说是灾难性的
佛罗里达州西棕榈滩——唐纳德·特朗普总统周四指责商务部在中期选举前故意发布不正确的经济增长数据，并表示他希望展开调查。
特朗普一再试图破坏人们对经济数据的信任，这些数据与他所声称的历史性繁荣不符，这种模式威胁到企业、金融市场和消费者在投资时所需数据的可信度。
他最新的投诉涉及商务部周三发布的数据，该数据将第三季度国内生产总值按年率修正为 4.3%，高于之前估计的 3.4%。
该部门的经济分析局定期更新其经济数据以提高其准确性。 GDP数据、月度就业报告和其他数据会定期修订。这些更新是按照预先安排的方式进行的，与政治日历无关。
但总统在社交媒体上声称这是一个“巨大的、有目的的错误”，并将其与共和党在 11 月 3 日中期选举中的糟糕表现联系起来，这次中期选举让民主党控制了国会参众两院。
特朗普发帖称：“刚刚透露，选举前公布的真实经济数据是假的，负责这些数据的政府机构的人员昨天发布了更正。” “为什么在选举前没有发布正确的号码？我要求立即调查这一情况。”
联邦官员称爱荷华州弹药爆炸后检测到“零”空气中的铅
感恩节风暴损坏了建筑物，淹没了街道，导致停电
“威胁终于成为现实”：法官驳斥白宫“武器化”
商务部没有立即回应置评请求。周四感恩节假期，政府基本关闭。
这是特朗普质疑他认为对他不利的经济数据完整性的最新实例，但没有提供证据表明修改是出于政治动机。 2025 年 8 月，特朗普在就业报告明显疲软后解雇了劳工统计局局长。该报告称，2025 年 7 月仅新增 73,000 个就业岗位，并显示 5 月和 6 月新增就业岗位比之前报告的少 258,000 个。
特朗普称这份就业报告“虚假”且“被操纵”。
特朗普声称，他因推动更强劲的经济增长而值得赞扬，但选民并不认同总统认为经济强劲的信念。根据美联社选民民意调查（对选民进行的一项广泛调查），在中期选举中，76％的人将经济状况描述为“不太好”或“很差”。大约三分之二的选民表示，特朗普自己的政策加剧了通货膨胀。
总统在社交媒体帖子中忽略了同一联邦机构周三还报告称，通胀的一个关键指标——个人消费支出价格指数——10月份年增长率加速至3.8%。

title_en: Newly released documents suggest CIA did more post-9/11 waterboarding than previously acknowledged
title_zh: 新发布的文件显示，中央情报局在 9/11 事件后实施的水刑比之前承认的还要多
summary: Declassified documents appear to support belief that waterboarding was more common and may have occurred beyond two acknowledged sites Newly released documents suggest that the CIA waterboarded more detainees during the post-9/11 “war on terror” than previousl
summary_zh: 解密文件似乎支持水刑更为常见的观点，并且可能发生在两个公认地点之外
body_en: Declassified documents appear to support belief that waterboarding was more common and may have occurred beyond two acknowledged sites

Newly released documents suggest that the CIA waterboarded more detainees during the post-9/11 “war on terror” than previously acknowledged, utilizing a site north of Kabul, Afghanistan , for the practice of simulated drowning.

The agency has acknowledged waterboarding three men: Abu Zubaydah, believed to be a high-ranking member of al-Qaida; Khalid Sheikh Mohammed, suspected architect of the 11 September 2001 attacks; and Abd al-Rahim al-Nashiri, accused of planning the 2000 bombing of a navy destroyer.

But declassified documents obtained under a freedom of information lawsuit by the New York Times , includes an account from a former CIA contract translator that appears to support the belief that waterboarding was more common and may have occurred beyond two acknowledged “special rendition” sites in Thailand and Poland.
The outlet reported on Friday that the linguist worked at a secret prison, or black site, one north of Kabul, Afghanistan, known as Salt Pit or Detention Site Cobalt.
The translator told an FBI agent in 2012 he had seen a man he called “Bahir” strapped to a board tilted downward into water.

“There were approximately three to four people ‘doing this,’” the FBI agent summarized in the account, saying that the witness “saw the incident in passing but did not participate himself. The waterboard session was in the hallway and there was not a lot of room.”

The account comes from an investigation into the CIA’s use of torture and its destruction of waterboarding videotapes from 2008 to 2012 conducted by then-special prosecutor John Durham. No charges were ever brought.
In the new documents produced by the Times , the linguist told the FBI in that “Bahir” was “a relative of Hekmatyar”, seemingly a reference to Gulbuddin Hekmatyar, the former Afghan prime minister.
That may correspond to a man named “Ghairat Bahir”, who was apprehended in a raid in Islamabad in 2002, appears in CIA records, and was subjected to “enhanced” interrogation techniques.
body_zh: 解密文件似乎支持水刑更为常见的观点，并且可能发生在两个公认地点之外
新公布的文件显示，在 9/11 事件后的“反恐战争”期间，中央情报局利用阿富汗喀布尔北部的一个地点进行模拟溺水练习，对被拘留者实施水刑，数量比之前承认的还要多。
该机构已承认对三名男子实施了水刑：阿布·祖巴伊达 (Abu Zubaydah)，据信是基地组织高级成员； Khalid Sheikh Mohammed，涉嫌策划 2001 年 9 月 11 日袭击事件；阿卜杜·拉希姆·纳什里 (Abd al-Rahim al-Nashiri) 被指控策划 2000 年轰炸一艘海军驱逐舰。
但《纽约时报》在信息自由诉讼中获得的解密文件中，包括一名前中央情报局合同翻译的叙述，该叙述似乎支持这样一种观点，即水刑更为普遍，而且可能发生在泰国和波兰两个公认的“特殊引渡”地点之外。
该媒体周五报道称，这名语言学家在阿富汗喀布尔北部的一处秘密监狱或黑色监狱工作，被称为“盐坑”或“钴拘留所”。
2012年，翻译告诉一名联邦调查局探员，他看到一名他称之为“巴希尔”的男子被绑在一块向下倾斜的木板上，浸入水中。
“大约有三到四个人‘这样做’，”联邦调查局特工在描述中总结道，并称目击者“路过看到了这一事件，但自己没有参与其中。水刑在走廊里进行，空间不大。”
该叙述来自时任特别检察官约翰·达勒姆 (John Durham) 对 2008 年至 2012 年间中央情报局使用酷刑和销毁水刑录像带的调查。从未提出任何指控。
在《泰晤士报》制作的新文件中，这位语言学家告诉联邦调查局，“巴希尔”是“希克马蒂亚尔的亲戚”，似乎指的是阿富汗前总理古尔布丁·希克马蒂亚尔。
这可能对应于一个名叫“Ghairat Bahir”的男子，他在 2002 年伊斯兰堡的一次突袭中被捕，出现在中央情报局的记录中，并受到了“强化”审讯手段。

title_en: U.S. Air Force cloud platform breached by hackers, report says
title_zh: 报告称美国空军云平台遭到黑客攻击
summary: The alleged incident follows a series of breaches and outages that have been reported at federal agencies this month.
summary_zh: 联邦机构本月报告了一系列违规和中断事件，之后发生了这起所谓的事件。
body_en: The U.S. Air Force's cloud computing platform was breached in a cyberattack, multiple sources told Reuters on Friday.
The hackers breached Cloud One, the Air Force's flagship cloud computing platform, according to Reuters, potentially exposing sensitive military and personnel information.
The breach was discovered at some point in the last month during system upgrades, sources told the outlet.

In a statement provided to CBS News, an Air Force spokesperson did not confirm or deny the breach, saying that it "does not comment on the security posture, vulnerabilities, or operational status of specific networks and systems."
"Ensuring the security, resilience and availability of our most critical war fighting assets remains a top priority," the Air Force spokesperson said.

In a follow-up statement, the Defense Department said that its systems "are safe, secure, and managed 24-7 by the best experts and teams in the world," adding that it "will continue to maintain all mission-critical operations and applications."

When reached by CBS News, Leidos, the tech company which has served as the main contractor operating Cloud One since May, declined to comment specifically on the hack, deferring to the Air Force. A Leidos spokesperson noted that earlier this year, it announced a $454.9 million contract to modernize and secure the Air Force's cloud operations.

The alleged incident follows a series of breaches and outages that have been reported at federal agencies this month, including at the National Security Agency, the CIA, the FBI, the U.S. Department of Agriculture, and the Federal Aviation Administration, the latter of which prompted a nationwide ground stop that triggered chaos for tens of thousands of travelers at U.S. airports.
In the FBI breach reported last week, hackers accessed a large database used by law enforcement agencies nationwide to access criminal records.

The NSA's network outage was linked to an urgent patching of vulnerabilities in PHP, the programming language that powers the majority of all websites, multiple sources told CBS News. The NSA's internal network, which is used to store and share classified information, went offline during the ordeal, the sources said.

The CIA and Office of the Director of National Intelligence, meanwhile, suffered an intrusion of an internal network that gathers intelligence from publicly available information, such as social media.
An ODNI official told CBS News in a statement Tuesday that there were "no disruptions to critical capabilities or classified systems" from that breach.

All this comes as White House National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross was fired from his position last week. Sources told CBS News that White House chief of staff Stephen Miller had long wanted Cairncross out of the job, and that he had told people he didn't think Cairncross had the expertise needed to be national cyber director.

title_en: Thanksgiving meal in Florida leads to mass food poisoning incident
title_zh: 佛罗里达州感恩节大餐引发大规模食物中毒事件
summary: Local media reported that 18 people fell ill after attending a Thanksgiving lunch at a medical center headquarters A Thanksgiving meal in Florida triggered a bout of food poisoning so bad that local emergency officials said it was a “mass casualty” event as nu
summary_zh: 当地媒体报道称，有 18 人在参加医疗中心总部的感恩节午餐后生病 佛罗里达州三地的感恩节大餐
body_en: Local media reported that 18 people fell ill after attending a Thanksgiving lunch at a medical center headquarters
A Thanksgiving meal in Florida triggered a bout of food poisoning so bad that local emergency officials said it was a “mass casualty” event as numerous stricken diners were sent to hospital.
Local media reported that 18 people at the Leon medical center headquarters in Doral fell ill due to possible food poisoning after attending the center’s annual Thanksgiving lunch on Wednesday.

Miami-Dade fire rescue crews who received reports of the possible food poisoning said the call was upgraded to a “ mass casualty incident ” after 15 of those who fell ill required hospitalization, the Miami Herald reported.
In a statement to NBC Miami Leon medical center said: “Some of the staff began to experience gastrointestinal symptoms shortly after the luncheon and required treatment.
“We continue to work with the caterers to determine, if possible, the cause and continue to provide support to our staff and their families.”
No patients at the center were affected. Investigations are continuing as to the exact cause and nature of the food poisoning.
body_zh: 当地媒体报道称，有 18 人在医疗中心总部参加感恩节午餐后生病
佛罗里达州的一顿感恩节大餐引发了一场严重的食物中毒，当地紧急官员称这是一次“大规模伤亡”事件，许多受伤的食客被送往医院。
当地媒体报道称，位于多拉尔的莱昂医疗中心总部周三有 18 人在参加该中心一年一度的感恩节午餐后因可能食物中毒而生病。
据《迈阿密先驱报》报道，收到可能食物中毒报告的迈阿密-戴德消防救援人员表示，在 15 名患病者需要住院治疗后，该事件已升级为“大规模伤亡事件”。
迈阿密莱昂医疗中心在给 NBC 的一份声明中表示：“午餐后不久，一些工作人员开始出现胃肠道症状，需要治疗。
“如果可能的话，我们将继续与餐饮服务商合作确定原因，并继续为我们的员工及其家人提供支持。”
该中心没有患者受到影响。关于食物中毒的确切原因和性质的调查仍在继续。

title_en: Bigfoot enthusiasts hope government’s US sightings files are ‘just the beginning’ of proving the creature real
title_zh: 大脚怪爱好者希望政府的美国目击档案只是证明这种生物真实性的“开始”
summary: The Forest Service’s work will ‘help normalize’ talk happening ‘for decades’, says ‘wood ape’ conservancy director When the Forest Service, one of the US government’s less sexy departments, quietly posted three documents to its website in mid-October, it was p
summary_zh: “木猿”保护主任表示，林业局的工作将“有助于使‘几十年来’发生的谈话正常化”。
body_en: The Forest Service’s work will ‘help normalize’ talk happening ‘for decades’, says ‘wood ape’ conservancy director
When the Forest Service, one of the US government’s less sexy departments, quietly posted three documents to its website in mid-October, it was probably hoping to avoid a fuss.

It didn’t succeed. The files were about Bigfoot, after all, and their publication sparked interest from around the globe, with Bigfoot enthusiasts hopeful that this could be a key step in the road to proving the creature is real.
US releases files on suspected Bigfoot sightings in Montana and Oregon

“It’s going to help normalize the conversation that the people in this community have been having for decades,” said Tami Grimes. She’s a director at the North American Wood Ape Conservancy (Nawac), which investigates sightings of Bigfoot (the organization prefers the term “wood ape”, as it is less mythical-sounding). Nawac collects reports and, if Bigfoot encounters are deemed legitimate, sends out volunteers to gather, or attempt to gather, evidence.
“The release of these papers shows that there have been government reports done to document it. It shows that there was enough to the incidents that the Forest Service took the incidents seriously.”

Grimes, 59, has reason to be invested. She said she had seen Bigfoot several times – the first when she was four years old. Her family lived close to Green Swamp, in central Florida, and Grimes recalls looking out of the bedroom one night and seeing a bipedal creature, covered in dark brown-to-black colored hair, staring back at her. It was 7ft tall, and powerfully built.

“The best way to describe the physique is that it was like Lou Ferrigno,” Grimes said, referring to the bodybuilder-turned-actor who was crowned Mr Universe in 1974 and later played the Hulk in the CBS TV show The Incredible Hulk.
“It was broad across the shoulders, incredibly muscular,” she said.

The creature, which Grimes believes was a Bigfoot, was not impeded by its bulky frame. It ran off at a “rapid speed”, Grimes recalls. She had nightmares for 25 years after the event. She then had another run-in with a Bigfoot in December 2003, when she and a friend went looking for one in a swamp in Florida. She saw a figure standing in the woods, swaying from side to side. It turned to look at her, Grimes said, then it tried and failed to hide behind a pine tree – “Its face and its backside was still sticking out from behind the tree” – before running off into the woods.
Grimes had been watching the figure through a thermal camera, but unfortunately she had only recently purchased the camera and did not know how to press record, so no footage was captured.

Bigfoot, or Sasquatch, has captured American imaginations for decades. Believers say the creature inhabits forests in the US and Canada, being particularly common in the Pacific north-west. Commonly described as tall, strong-looking and foul-smelling, there have been thousands of reports of sightings submitted to amateur Bigfoot tracking organizations like Nawac and the Bigfoot Field Researchers Organization.

Yet Bigfoot is considered by many to be a myth, its alleged existence attributable to folk tales and whimsy, and governmental discussion of it is rare. The White House, the US Department of Defense and the US Department of the Interior all declined to comment on Bigfoot to the Guardian.

The Forest Service did reply. In a statement, a spokesman said: “Stories of Bigfoot, Sasquatch, and other legendary beings have long been part of the cultural fabric of many regions, reflecting a rich tradition of folklore, oral history, and storytelling that surrounds our public lands. While the Forest Service does not endorse or make any claims regarding the existence of such creatures, we appreciate the public’s enthusiasm for exploring and learning about our public lands.”

Other sources were more forthright. A chatbot on the National Park Service website said there “is no scientific evidence that Bigfoot exists as a real animal”, while Encyclopedia Britannica said “most scientists do not recognize the creature’s existence”. Bigfoot does not feature in the National Wildlife Federation’s database of fauna found in the US.
Sasquatch ‘sightings’ reignite fervour and scepticism about ape-like beast

The number of Bigfoot hoaxes probably hasn’t helped boost its credibility. In one case, two men said they found a Bigfoot body, but when they handed it over to researchers it turned out to be a rubber gorilla suit. A 2014 study of 30 hair samples alleged to be yeti or Bigfoot found that all the hair was from extant species, including a black bear, a cow and a human.

Still, there was plenty of excitement when the forestry service quietly released those Bigfoot-related documents, even if the content was a little underwhelming. One of the files was merely a copy of a newspaper article, which reported that mysterious tracks had been discovered in Montana. Another was a 1980 essay written by someone called Leo Kinney , in which Kinney wrote that he and three others had encountered something in the woods: a creature “that walked on its hind legs that altho [sic] there wasn’t actual sightings, tracks, a strong odor and a gruntling sound were observed”.

The file that received the most attention was probably a report which had been commissioned by the US Department of Agriculture. In the report, Rodney Johnson, a wildlife biologist, said the USDA had asked him to accompany a group in the Umatilla national forest, in Portland, to investigate a reported finding of Bigfoot tracks – suggesting that at least someone at the department thought Bigfoot worthy of further study.
body_zh: “木猿”保护主任表示，林业局的工作将“帮助使‘几十年来’发生的谈话正常化”
当美国政府不太性感的部门之一林务局于 10 月中旬悄悄在其网站上发布三份文件时，它可能希望避免大惊小怪。
但没有成功。毕竟，这些文件是关于大脚怪的，它们的出版引起了全球各地的兴趣，大脚怪爱好者希望这可能是证明这种生物真实存在的关键一步。
美国公布蒙大拿州和俄勒冈州疑似大脚怪目击事件的文件
塔米·格里姆斯说：“这将有助于使这个社区的人们几十年来一直进行的对话正常化。”她是北美木猿保护协会（Nawac）的主任，该组织负责调查大脚怪的目击事件（该组织更喜欢“木猿”这个词，因为它听起来不那么神秘）。纳瓦克收集报告，如果大脚怪遭遇被认为是合法的，他会派出志愿者收集或试图收集证据。
“这些文件的发布表明，已经有政府报告对此进行了记录。这表明林业局认真对待了这些事件。”
59 岁的格莱姆斯有理由进行投资。她说她见过大脚怪好几次——第一次是在她四岁时。她的家人住在佛罗里达州中部的格林沼泽附近，格莱姆斯回忆说，有一天晚上，她从卧室向外望去，看到一个双足生物，全身覆盖着深棕色到黑色的头发，正在回望着她。它高 7 英尺，结构坚固。
“描述体格的最好方式就是像卢·费里尼奥 (Lou Ferrigno)，”格莱姆斯说。他指的是这位从健美运动员转型为演员的演员，他于 1974 年加冕宇宙先生，后来在 CBS 电视节目《绿巨人浩克》中扮演绿巨人。
“它的肩膀很宽，肌肉非常发达，”她说。
格莱姆斯认为这种生物是大脚怪，但它庞大的身躯并没有妨碍它。格莱姆斯回忆道，它以“极快的速度”逃跑。事件发生后的25年里，她一直做噩梦。 2003 年 12 月，当她和一位朋友在佛罗里达州的沼泽地里寻找大脚怪时，她又与大脚怪发生了冲突。她看到树林里站着一个人影，左右摇晃。格莱姆斯说，它转身看着她，然后试图躲在一棵松树后面，但失败了——“它的脸和背面仍然从树后面伸出来”——然后跑进了树林。
格莱姆斯一直通过热感摄像机观察这个人影，但遗憾的是她最近才购买摄像机，不知道如何按记录，所以没有拍摄到镜头。
几十年来，大脚怪或大脚野人一直吸引着美国人的想象力。信徒们说，这种生物栖息在美国和加拿大的森林中，在太平洋西北部尤其常见。通常被描述为身材高大、外表强壮、气味难闻，已有数千份目击大脚怪的报告提交给了纳瓦克和大脚怪野外研究组织等业余大脚怪追踪组织。
然而，许多人认为大脚怪是一个神话，其所谓的存在归因于民间故事和奇思妙想，政府对它的讨论很少。白宫、美国国防部和美国内政部均拒绝向《卫报》发表评论。
林务局确实回复了。一位发言人在一份声明中表示：“大脚怪、大脚野人和其他传奇生物的故事长期以来一直是许多地区文化结构的一部分，反映了我们公共土地周围丰富的民间传说、口述历史和讲故事的传统。虽然林务局不认可或对这些生物的存在做出任何声明，但我们赞赏公众探索和了解我们公共土地的热情。”
其他消息来源则更为直率。国家公园管理局网站上的聊天机器人表示，“没有科学证据表明大脚怪作为真正的动物存在”，而大英百科全书则表示“大多数科学家不承认这种生物的存在”。大脚怪并未出现在美国国家野生动物联盟的动物群数据库中。
大脚野人的“目击事件”重新点燃了人们对类人猿野兽的热情和怀疑
大脚怪恶作剧的数量可能并没有帮助提高其可信度。在一个案例中，两名男子说他们发现了一具大脚怪的尸体，但当他们将其交给研究人员时，结果发现它是一件橡胶大猩猩套装。 2014 年对 30 个据称是雪人或大脚怪的头发样本进行的研究发现，所有头发都来自现存物种，包括黑熊、牛和人类。
尽管如此，当林业部门悄悄发布那些与大脚怪相关的文件时，尽管内容有点平淡，但还是引起了人们的兴奋。其中一份文件只是一篇报纸文章的副本，该文章报道在蒙大拿州发现了神秘的足迹。另一篇是 1980 年由一位名叫 Leo Kinney 的人写的文章，其中 Kinney 写道，他和另外三个人在树林里遇到了一些东西：一种“用后腿行走的生物，尽管没有实际的目击、足迹、强烈的气味和咕噜声”。
最受关注的文件可能是美国农业部委托编写的一份报告。野生动物生物学家罗德尼·约翰逊在报告中表示，美国农业部要求他陪同波特兰尤马蒂拉国家森林中的一个小组去调查据报道发现的大脚怪足迹，这表明该部门至少有人认为大脚怪值得进一步研究。

title_en: Court lets Puerto Rico governor fire firm that runs the island's troubled power grid
title_zh: 法院允许波多黎各州长解雇经营该岛陷入困境的电网的公司

body_en: Court lets Puerto Rico governor fire firm that runs the island's troubled power grid LUMA Energy took over the electric grid five years ago. The court's ruling nullifies its contract, and gives the government a year to find a new operator.
Puerto Rico Supreme Court allows governor to fire company that runs the island's troubled power grid
LUMA Energy took over the electric grid five years ago. The court's ruling nullifies its contract, and gives the government a year to find a new operator.

Puerto Rico's supreme court has ruled the island's governor can kick out the private company that's been running its troubled power grid for five years. The decision could have huge consequences for electric service in Puerto Rico. Here is NPR's Adrian Florido.

ADRIAN FLORIDO, BYLINE: After Hurricane Maria flattened Puerto Rico's already rickety power grid in 2017, the island's government privatized it. It gave a company called LUMA Energy, based in Canada and Texas, a 15-year deal to take over the power lines, promising that LUMA would rebuild the grid stronger and improve the notoriously unreliable service. LUMA took over in 2021. But things have not gone as planned.

Blackouts are still a constant fact of life. LUMA has come in for harsh criticism from customers and officials. Last year, Governor Jenniffer Gonzalez-Colon filed suit to nullify LUMA's contract. Yesterday, the Puerto Rican Supreme Court ruled in her favor that LUMA must go.
JENNIFFER GONZALEZ-COLON: Today is a day of celebration on the island.
FLORIDO: This is the governor speaking after the ruling. She said LUMA has not lived up to its promises.
GONZALEZ-COLON: More outages on the island, more shutdowns on the island. They have not fulfilled the requirements of the contract.

FLORIDO: In fact, the island's supreme court ruled on procedural grounds, saying officials had not followed local requirements when approving agreements with the company. The court gave the local government a year to put a new operator in place. The governor said the work to find a new private company will start immediately.

GONZALEZ-COLON: It's going to be a good transition. We're going to make it in a year. And I hope that all companies that are interested in participating in this process will fulfill and follow the process of law. And we're going to be opening that process for public bid.

FLORIDO: The court gave LUMA Energy 10 days to request a reconsideration of its ruling. In a statement, LUMA said it is considering its legal options. The company has long argued that the grid it took over was in awful shape and that it is not fully to blame for the blackouts. A new operator will need approval from both the local government and a federal oversight board that Congress put in place 10 years ago to get Puerto Rico out of bankruptcy. In a statement, that board criticized the governor for ending LUMA' s contract without having a new company ready to go. It said it's worried about the continuity of service on the island. In her remarks yesterday, the governor said she has a plan in place and will reveal it soon.

五年前，LUMA Energy 接管了电网。法院的裁决使其合同无效，并给政府一年的时间寻找新的运营商。
波多黎各最高法院裁定，该岛州长可以将这家运营其陷入困境的电网五年的私人公司驱逐出境。这一决定可能会对波多黎各的电力服务产生巨大影响。请听 NPR 的阿德里安·弗洛里多的报道。
阿德里安·弗洛里多连线：2017 年，飓风玛丽亚摧毁了波多黎各本已摇摇欲坠的电网，该岛政府将其私有化。它向一家总部位于加拿大和德克萨斯州、名为 LUMA Energy 的公司提供了一份为期 15 年的接管电力线路的协议，并承诺 LUMA 将重建更强大的电网并改善众所周知的不可靠服务。 LUMA 于 2021 年接手。但事情并没有按计划进行。
停电仍然是生活中常见的事实。 LUMA 受到了客户和官员的严厉批评。去年，州长 Jenniffer Gonzalez-Colon 提起诉讼，要求取消 LUMA 的合同。昨天，波多黎各最高法院做出了对她有利的裁决，LUMA 必须下台。
JENNIFFER GONZALEZ-COLON：今天是岛上庆祝的一天。
弗洛里多：这是州长在裁决后发表的讲话。她说 LUMA 没有兑现其承诺。
冈萨雷斯-科隆：岛上停电更多，岛上停工更多。他们没有履行合同的要求。
佛罗里达州：事实上，该岛最高法院以程序为由作出裁决，称官员在批准与该公司的协议时没有遵循当地要求。法院给了当地政府一年的时间来任命新的运营商。州长表示，寻找新私营公司的工作将立即开始。
冈萨雷斯-科隆：这将是一个很好的过渡。我们将在一年内做到这一点。我希望所有有兴趣参与这一过程的公司都履行并遵守法律程序。我们将开放该流程进行公开招标。

佛罗里达州：法院给 LUMA Energy 10 天的时间要求重新考虑其裁决。 LUMA 在一份声明中表示，正在考虑采取法律选择。该公司长期以来一直辩称，它接管的电网状况很糟糕，停电事件不能完全归咎于它。新的运营商需要得到当地政府和联邦监督委员会的批准，该委员会是国会十年前为帮助波多黎各摆脱破产而设立的。在一份声明中，该董事会批评州长在没有准备好新公司的情况下就终止了 LUMA 的合同。它表示担心岛上服务的连续性。州长在昨天的讲话中表示，她已经制定了计划，并将很快公布。

body_en: Iran War Updates: U.S. forces disable commercial ship that allegedly tried to breach blockade on Iranian ports

U.S. forces used precision munitions to disable a commercial vessel that allegedly tried to breach the American blockade of Iranian ports, U.S. Central Command said Friday. The U.S. military said the ship's crew was given multiple warnings before the strike, and that crew members were unharmed.

President Trump said Thursday that victory in the war with Iran would be achieved "whenever I want it," and that he is giving the Islamic Republic's regime "a chance to be smart," though he said he doubts they will take it.

Mr. Trump also downplayed the importance of Russia and China's intelligence sharing with Iran after multiple reports that Tehran's allies have helped it target U.S. military assets in the Middle East.
8:10 PM U.N. says hunger is expected to worsen in Yemen
Hunger is expected to worsen in 16 countries over the next six months, with war-torn Sudan and Yemen among five nations facing the gravest risk, the United Nations' food agencies warned Friday.

The agencies pointed to conflict, soaring fuel costs linked to war in the Middle East and steep cuts in aid. The Food and Agriculture Organization and the World Food Program's Hunger Hotspots report covers December through May 2026.

It places Sudan, Yemen, South Sudan, Somalia and northern Nigeria at the highest level of concern. In Yemen, the report said, hunger is likely to worsen as fighting that resumed in July spreads across multiple fronts.

All five have appeared on the list repeatedly since 2022. The Palestinian territories were moved down one level following the October 2025 ceasefire in Gaza, though 67% of Gaza's population still faces crisis-level hunger or worse, and the report warned that the gains were fragile.
Yemen has been at war since 2014, when the Iran-backed Houthi rebels seized the capital, Sanaa, prompting a Saudi-led coalition to intervene the following year.

The Houthis' encirclement of the southwestern city of Taiz has created siege-like conditions there, and more than 300,000 people have been displaced since the escalation began in July, mostly in Taiz, Lahj and Aden provinces. In government-held areas, 1.8 million people face emergency levels of hunger, up from 1.6 million in the previous analysis.

No recent assessment exists for areas held by the Houthis, which have become harder for aid groups to reach as the conflict has intensified. The last nationwide projection, which ran through February, found 18.3 million people, more than half the population, in crisis or worse.

Yemen relies heavily on imported food and fuel, and the report warned that attacks on Red Sea shipping threaten that lifeline. Shipping is now disrupted in the Strait of Hormuz, the Red Sea and the Black Sea. Gulf fertilizer shipments remain largely halted.

body_zh: 伊朗战争最新消息：美军摧毁了据称试图突破伊朗港口封锁的商船
美国中央司令部周五表示，美军使用精确弹药摧毁了一艘据称试图突破美国对伊朗港口封锁的商船。美国军方表示，袭击发生前，该船的船员多次收到警告，但船员没有受伤。
特朗普总统周四表示，“只要我愿意”，就能在与伊朗的战争中取得胜利，并且他正在给伊朗伊斯兰共和国政权“一个聪明的机会”，尽管他表示怀疑他们是否会接受这个机会。
在多份报道称德黑兰的盟友帮助其瞄准美国在中东的军事资产后，特朗普还淡化了俄罗斯和中国与伊朗共享情报的重要性。
晚上 8:10 联合国称也门的饥饿状况预计将恶化
联合国粮食机构周五警告称，未来六个月内，预计 16 个国家的饥饿状况将进一步恶化，其中饱受战争蹂躏的苏丹和也门是面临最严重风险的五个国家之一。
这些机构指出了冲突、与中东战争有关的燃料成本飙升以及援助大幅削减等问题。联合国粮食及农业组织和世界粮食计划署的饥饿热点报告涵盖 2026 年 12 月至 5 月。
苏丹、也门、南苏丹、索马里和尼日利亚北部受到最严重的关注。报告称，在也门，随着七月恢复的战斗蔓延到多个战线，饥饿可能会恶化。
自 2022 年以来，这五个国家都多次出现在名单上。2025 年 10 月加沙停火后，巴勒斯坦领土下降了一级，尽管加沙 67% 的人口仍然面临危机级别的饥饿或更严重的情况，报告警告称，取得的进展很脆弱。
也门自2014年以来一直处于战争状态，当时伊朗支持的胡塞叛军占领了首都萨那，促使沙特领导的联盟于次年进行干预。
胡塞武装对西南城市塔伊兹的包围造成了那里的围困，自7月份冲突升级以来已有超过30万人流离失所，其中大部分在塔伊兹省、拉赫吉省和亚丁省。在政府控制的地区，有 180 万人面临紧急饥饿水平，高于之前分析中的 160 万人。
最近没有对胡塞武装控制地区进行评估，随着冲突加剧，援助团体越来越难以到达这些地区。 2 月份进行的最新全国预测发现，有 1,830 万人（占总人口的一半以上）处于危机或更严重的境地。
也门严重依赖进口食品和燃料，报告警告说，对红海航运的袭击威胁着这一生命线。霍尔木兹海峡、红海和黑海的航运现已中断。海湾地区化肥运输仍基本停止。
2026 年 11 月 27 日下午 3:08 巴基斯坦和土耳其誓言支持沙特阿拉伯抵御伊朗支持的胡塞武装的袭击
巴基斯坦和土耳其誓言支持沙特阿拉伯，打击伊朗支持的也门胡塞叛军的持续袭击，这三个国家周五根据三边防御协议举行了会谈，该协议将对一个成员的攻击视为对所有成员的攻击。
巴基斯坦外交部长伊沙克·达尔在电视讲话中表示，会议同意继续支持旨在缓和地区紧张局势的努力，并鼓励通过对话和外交和平解决争端。
土耳其官员表示，安卡拉正在考虑向沙特阿拉伯提供军事援助，但坚称麦加联合防御协议是防御性的，土耳其不会部署军队在也门作战或攻击胡塞武装。
巴基斯坦也称该协议纯粹是防御性的，称该协议不针对包括伊朗在内的任何国家，反映了加强战略安全合作的共同愿望。

title_en: 2 American Airlines jets clip wings on tarmac of Reagan Airport
title_zh: 两架美国航空喷气式飞机在里根机场停机坪上折断机翼
summary: There were no injuries when the wingtips of two American Airlines jets made contact Friday evening on the tarmac of Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport outside Washington, D.C.
summary_zh: 周五晚上，美国航空的两架飞机在罗纳德·里根华盛顿国家机场的停机坪上发生接触，没有造成人员伤亡
body_en: There were no injuries when the wingtips of two American Airlines jets made contact Friday evening on the tarmac of Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport outside Washington, D.C., officials said.

American Airlines Flight 638 clipped the wing of American Airlines Flight 2152 a little after 5 p.m. local time while both aircraft were taxiing for departure, according to the Federal Aviation Administration.
In a separate statement provided to CBS News, American Airlines said that both planes returned to their gates and were "removed from service for inspection by our maintenance team."
Both the FAA and American Airlines said no injuries were reported.

The Metropolitan Washington Airports Authority said in a statement that its fire and rescue personnel responded to both planes. The airports authority said there were no disruptions to any other flights.
Flight 638 was bound for Dallas, while Flight 2152 was headed to Chicago. The airline said passengers would be placed on new planes and depart for their destinations later Friday night.
Earlier this month , two passengers suffered minor injuries when the wingtip of a Copa Airlines jet struck the nose of a UPS cargo plane on the tarmac of Miami International Airport.
And in early October, the left wingtip of a Delta Air Lines plane clipped the tail of an Air Canada aircraft on the tarmac of Los Angeles International Airport. There were no injuries.
Reagan Airport has three runways, one of which is considered the busiest in the nation, and it operates with a tightly restricted airspace due to its location near the White House and Capitol Hill.

In January 2025 , an Army Black Hawk helicopter collided in midair with an American Airlines plane that was approaching to land at Reagan Airport. All 64 people aboard the American Airlines flight were killed, along with the three soldiers aboard the chopper.

title_en: U.S. Judge rules FCC violated ABC's free speech rights to please Trump
title_zh: 美国法官裁定 FCC 侵犯 ABC 的言论自由权以取悦特朗普
summary: A federal judge has blocked the Trump administration from moving to review all local broadcast licenses held by ABC. The stations air in six of the largest U.S. markets.
summary_zh: 一名联邦法官阻止特朗普政府审查美国广播公司持有的所有当地广播许可证。该电台在其中六个地区播出
body_en: U.S. Judge: FCC violated ABC’s free speech to please Trump : NPR

U.S. Judge: FCC violated ABC’s free speech to please Trump A federal judge has blocked the Trump administration from moving to review all local broadcast licenses held by ABC. The stations air in six of the largest U.S. markets.

Under Chairman Brendan Carr, left, the Federal Communications Commission launched an early review of Disney's licenses to operate all the local ABC stations it owns. New Disney CEO Josh D'Amaro, right, says the company is fighting back to protect ABC's journalistic integrity and free speech. "We're very principled on this," he said. Heather Diehl/Thibault Camus/Pool/AFP via Getty Images hide caption

A federal judge has blocked President Trump and his administration from taking action to challenge the ABC television network's broadcast licenses, finding it to be an unconstitutional punishment for satire, commentary and news coverage that Trump doesn't like.
Disney, ABC battle Trump's FCC in court over free speech protections

In her preliminary injunction filed Wednesday, U.S. District Court Judge Loren AliKhan found that the federal agency's early reviews represented retaliation for speech the Trump administration resented.

Such perceived offenses included late-night host Jimmy Kimmel's jabs at the president, the critical remarks of hosts on the chat show The View , and the moderation of a presidential debate in September 2024.

ABC and its corporate parent, the Walt Disney Co., serve six of the 10 largest markets in the U.S., including New York, Los Angeles, and Houston. They contribute significantly to the network's bottom line.

"Given the extreme, indeed existential, nature of the possible penalty Plaintiffs face -- loss of their broadcast licenses -- the court concludes that early license renewal proceedings create a risk sufficient to chill a broadcaster of ordinary firmness," Judge AliKhan wrote.

She rejected the Trump administration's motion to dismiss the lawsuit from ABC and Disney challenging the review of the local licenses. Usually the licenses last eight years and are up for review on a staggered basis. They are rarely taken away.

In her ruling, AliKhan relied heavily on public statements and social media postings in which Trump attacked ABC and Disney, as well as posts by Trump's pick as the chair of the Federal Communications Commission, Brendan Carr.

"What started in 2020 as questions about how ABC 'can keep getting a license' if it 'report[s] fake news,' ... has crescendoed into repeated calls for the Commission to strip ABC's broadcast licenses for their editorial decisions," she wrote. "The court counts eleven such calls made by President Trump over the past two years -- the most recent being in July 2026."
And the judge cited the administration's "tangible steps toward enforcing President Trump and Commissioner Carr's repeated threats to strip the Plaintiff Stations of their licenses."
"Chairman Carr has taken President Trump's rhetoric as his marching orders," Judge AliKhan wrote.
Carr did not respond to NPR's request for comment Wednesday evening.
ABC hailed the ruling in a statement as "an important victory for the First Amendment."

Among the targets of ire from Trump and Carr was ABC's decision not to broadcast Trump's July 2026 Oval Office address on its television network. ABC's legal team said the network streamed it on its digital news service, but would not have done so absent the political pressure from the FCC.

It is one of several examples of newsroom decisions made under duress, the network's lawyers said in court. Kimmel's interview with then-Democratic U.S. Senate nominee James Talarico of Texas was uploaded to YouTube instead of being aired on ABC's late night television show. (Talarico won election to the U.S. Senate earlier this month.) And The View stopped hosting candidates for political office in 2026 in the months ahead of the fall elections.
body_zh: 美国法官：FCC为了取悦特朗普而侵犯了ABC的言论自由 : NPR
美国法官：FCC为了取悦特朗普而侵犯ABC的言论自由 一名联邦法官阻止特朗普政府审查ABC持有的所有当地广播许可证。这些电台在美国六个最大的市场播出。
在主席布伦丹·卡尔（左）的领导下，联邦通信委员会对迪士尼拥有的所有当地 ABC 电视台的运营许可证进行了早期审查。迪士尼新任首席执行官乔什·达马罗（右）表示，公司正在反击，以保护 ABC 的新闻诚信和言论自由。 “我们对此非常有原则，”他说。 Heather Diehl/Thibault Camus/Pool/法新社来自 Getty Images 隐藏标题栏
一名联邦法官阻止特朗普总统及其政府采取行动挑战美国广播公司电视网络的广播许可证，认为这是对特朗普不喜欢的讽刺、评论和新闻报道的违宪惩罚。
迪士尼和美国广播公司 (ABC) 在法庭上就言论自由保护问题与特朗普的联邦通信委员会 (FCC) 展开斗争
美国地方法院法官洛伦·阿里汗在周三提交的初步禁令中发现，联邦机构的早期审查是对特朗普政府不满的言论的报复。
此类被视为冒犯的行为包括深夜主持人吉米·金梅尔对总统的攻击、主持人在脱口秀节目《The View》中的批评言论，以及对 2024 年 9 月总统辩论的缓和。
ABC 及其母公司华特迪士尼公司为美国 10 个最大市场中的 6 个提供服务，包括纽约、洛杉矶和休斯顿。它们对网络的盈利做出了重大贡献。
法官写道：“鉴于原告可能面临的惩罚的极端性，甚至是生死攸关的性质——失去广播许可证——法院的结论是，过早的许可证续签程序所造成的风险足以让一家普通的广播公司感到不寒而栗。”
她拒绝了特朗普政府驳回美国广播公司和迪士尼对当地许可审查提出质疑的诉讼的动议。通常，许可证的有效期为八年，并且会分阶段接受审查。他们很少被带走。
阿里汗在裁决中严重依赖特朗普攻击美国广播公司和迪士尼的公开声明和社交媒体帖子，以及特朗普任命的联邦通信委员会主席布伦丹·卡尔的帖子。
她写道：“从 2020 年开始，人们开始质疑 ABC 如果‘报道假新闻’，如何‘能够继续获得许可证’……现在已经逐渐演变成一再呼吁委员会取消 ABC 因其编辑决定而获得的广播许可证。” “法院统计特朗普总统在过去两年中发出了 11 次此类电话——最近一次是在 2026 年 7 月。”
法官还援引了政府“为执行特朗普总统和卡尔专员一再威胁吊销原告电视台执照而采取的切实步骤”。
阿里汗法官写道：“卡尔主席已将特朗普总统的言论作为他的行军命令。”
周三晚上，卡尔没有回应 NPR 的置评请求。
美国广播公司在一份声明中称赞这一裁决是“第一修正案的重要胜利”。
特朗普和卡尔愤怒的目标之一是美国广播公司 (ABC) 决定不在其电视网络上播出特朗普 2026 年 7 月在椭圆形办公室的讲话。美国广播公司的法律团队表示，该网络在其数字新闻服务上播放了该节目，但如果没有联邦通信委员会的政治压力，美国广播公司不会这样做。
该网络的律师在法庭上表示，这是新闻编辑室在胁迫下做出决定的几个例子之一。基梅尔对当时的美国民主党参议员候选人、来自德克萨斯州的詹姆斯·塔拉里科的采访被上传到 YouTube，而不是在美国广播公司的深夜电视节目中播出。 （塔拉里科本月早些时候赢得了美国参议院选举。）在秋季选举前的几个月，The View 停止接待 2026 年政治职务候选人。

title_zh: 加拿大最高法院基本维持魁北克禁止公务员使用宗教标志的禁令
summary: The 2019 law, known as Bill 21, bans religious symbols — including Muslim headscarves, Sikh turbans, Jewish skullcaps and Christian crosses — for workers covered by it.
summary_zh: 2019 年的法律（即第 21 号法案）禁止​​在工作中佩戴宗教标志，包括穆斯林头巾、锡克教头巾、犹太无边帽和基督教十字架
body_en: Rob Gillies, Associated Press Rob Gillies, Associated Press
https://www.pbs.org/newshour/world/canadas-supreme-court-largely-upholds-a-quebec-ban-on-religious-symbols-for-public-servants

TORONTO (AP) — Canada's Supreme Court on Friday upheld most of a Quebec law banning public schoolteachers, police officers and other public employees in positions of authority from wearing religious symbols at work. The ruling affirmed Quebec's power to override certain constitutional rights to keep the ban in place.
The 2019 law, known as Bill 21, bans religious symbols — including Muslim headscarves, Sikh turbans, Jewish skullcaps and Christian crosses — for workers covered by it.

Canada has long embraced multiculturalism, encouraging people to retain their cultural and religious identities. Supporters of Quebec's ban say public officials should avoid wearing religious symbols to demonstrate government neutrality.
Quebec Premier Paul St-Pierre Plamondon welcomed the ruling as "a victory for secularism" and for Quebec's ability to make different choices from the rest of Canada.

The court upheld Quebec's use of the "notwithstanding clause," which allows lawmakers to override certain rights, including religious freedom and equality. Those rights are protected by the Charter of Rights and Freedoms, Canada's equivalent of the U.S. Bill of Rights. Lawmakers must renew the override every five years to keep it in effect.

Prime Minister Mark Carney said he respected the ruling but pledged that his government would not use the constitutional override. He stressed that constitutional rights are particularly important for minorities and vulnerable people.
"Canada is a mosaic," Carney said, adding that it represents more than different backgrounds and identities. "It's a commitment, in my judgment, a commitment to how we treat each other."

Carney also welcomed the court's finding that judges can still declare that a law violates constitutional rights even when the override allows it to remain in force. He said that scrutiny helps inform Canadians and is useful in a democracy.
Chief Justice Richard Wagner wrote that the law reflected Quebec's "legitimate and historical commitment" to keeping government secular.
The court maintained an exemption allowing members of Quebec's legislature to cover their heads — or potentially, for women, to cover their faces — while performing their duties.
Quebec's commitment to secularism grew from its rejection of the Roman Catholic Church's once-dominant influence.
Opponents say the law discriminates against religious minorities, particularly Muslim women who wear headscarves.
"Quebec is still telling qualified people that they must set aside their faith," said Mehramat Kaur of the World Sikh Organization of Canada.
France, Belgium, Austria and the Netherlands have full or partial bans on face coverings, including veils worn by some Muslim women.
Other Canadian provinces have used the override for laws restricting transgender rights or ordering striking employees back to work.
Manitoba Premier Wab Kinew called Bill 21 "legislated discrimination" against Muslims, Sikhs and other religious minorities. He said his government would never use the override.

多伦多（美联社）——加拿大最高法院周五维持了魁北克省一项法律的大部分内容，该法律禁止公立学校教师、警察和其他担任要职的公职人员在工作中佩戴宗教标志。该裁决确认了魁北克有权推翻某些宪法权利以维持禁令。
2019 年的法律（称为第 21 号法案）禁止​​员工佩戴宗教标志，包括穆斯林头巾、锡克教头巾、犹太无边帽和基督教十字架。
加拿大长期以来一直拥护多元文化主义，鼓励人们保留自己的文化和宗教身份。魁北克禁令的支持者表示，公职人员应避免佩戴宗教标志以表明政府中立。
魁北克省省长保罗·圣皮埃尔·普拉蒙东 (Paul St-Pierre Plamondon) 对这一裁决表示欢迎，称其为“世俗主义的胜利”，并认为魁北克有能力做出与加拿大其他地区不同的选择。
法院支持魁北克省使用“尽管条款”，该条款允许立法者推翻某些权利，包括宗教自由和平等。这些权利受到《权利与自由宪章》的保护，加拿大相当于美国的《权利法案》。立法者必须每五年更新一次优先权以使其生效。
总理马克·卡尼表示，他尊重这一裁决，但承诺他的政府不会动用宪法推翻的权力。他强调，宪法权利对于少数群体和弱势群体尤为重要。
“加拿大是一个马赛克，”卡尼说，并补充说，它代表的不仅仅是不同的背景和身份。 “在我看来，这是一种承诺，是对我们如何对待彼此的承诺。”
卡尼还对法院的裁决表示欢迎，即即使推翻法律允许该法律继续有效，法官仍然可以宣布该法律侵犯了宪法权利。他说，审查有助于加拿大人了解情况，并且对民主国家很有用。
首席大法官理查德·瓦格纳写道，该法律反映了魁北克对保持政府世俗化的“合法和历史承诺”。
法院维持了一项豁免，允许魁北克立法机构成员在履行职责时遮盖头部，或者对于女性来说，可以遮盖面部。
魁北克对世俗主义的承诺源于其对罗马天主教会一度占主导地位的影响的拒绝。
反对者表示，该法律歧视宗教少数群体，特别是戴头巾的穆斯林妇女。
加拿大世界锡克教组织的迈赫拉马特·考尔（Mehramat Kaur）表示：“魁北克仍在告诉合格的人，他们必须放弃自己的信仰。”
法国、比利时、奥地利和荷兰全面或部分禁止佩戴面部遮盖物，包括一些穆斯林妇女佩戴的面纱。
加拿大其他省份也利用了限制变性人权利或命令罢工员工重返工作岗位的法律的优先权。
马尼托巴省省长瓦布·基纽 (Wab Kinew) 称第 21 号法案是对穆斯林、锡克教徒和其他宗教少数群体的“立法歧视”。他表示，他的政府永远不会使用这一优先权。

title_en: Cenk Uygur goes all in on Ro Khanna for 2028
title_zh: Cenk Uygur 全力支持 Ro Khanna 2028 年比赛
summary: Khanna got a "Cenksgiving" surprise on Hasan Piker's stream.
summary_zh: 卡纳在哈桑·派克的直播中收到了“Cenksgiving”惊喜。
body_en: Ro Khanna hasn't launched a 2028 bid yet, but he already has a pioneer of the populist left in his corner.

Progressive firebrand Cenk Uygur is set to formally endorse the California Democrat on Thursday night during his annual appearance on nephew Hasan Piker's Twitch stream, a Thanksgiving Day debate-a-thon the pair call "Cenksgiving." Uygur told POLITICO he will pitch Khanna as the best populist progressive candidate. His Rebellion PAC will also debut its first 2028 ad promoting a Khanna candidacy Thursday night.
"For me, it's a no-brainer," Uygur said in an interview, explaining why he’s backing Khanna. "Who else would you back, and why would any progressive or any populist back anyone else?"

Along with his PAC getting behind Khanna, Uygur is also launching his own "Draft Ro" website to collect signatures and showcase other early high-profile endorsers, though he wouldn't say who just yet.

The endorsement is one of the first of the 2028 cycle, and it comes before any major candidate has formally announced. Inside Washington, Khanna’s chances are viewed as quite slim. But for Uygur, that kind of underestimation is exactly part of the draw.
"I love it," Uygur said of the skepticism. "I wouldn't have backed him if anyone in D.C. was behind him."
"We're running against Washington," he added. "So if Washington doesn't like a candidate, perfect."

Uygur is pairing his endorsement with a litmus test he’s trying to lay down for 2028 progressives: Candidates must call what Israel has done in Gaza a genocide and support ending U.S. funding for Israel. "It isn't actually about Israel," Uygur said. "It's about: Is this person going to represent us or not?"

Khanna, he said, is "among the very, very few, and maybe the only candidate, that'll pass that test." He allowed for one other: "There's also AOC. If she runs, that's another person that could pass the test."

But that's as far as the praise goes. His endorsement of Khanna comes as many other progressives are waiting to see whether Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (D-N.Y.) jumps in. Uygur isn't one of them. Asked if her entry would change his calculus, he said: "Not 1%."
"Sorry, but I don't think AOC means it," he said. "I don't think she would do any of the things that she says, and so I'm not going to back someone who is not going to deliver."
"She's obsessed with the establishment, so she's going to run a soft, weak race," he added. "She wants to make Democratic leaders and mainstream media happy. Good luck with that strategy."
Khanna has told POLITICO he plans to decide whether to run after the holidays and that whether Ocasio-Cortez gets in won't factor into his decision.

Uygur's backing could give the potential 2028 candidate some credibility on the populist left, not to mention a boost from "The Young Turks," one of the longest-running and most popular progressive shows online, which Uygur launched in 2002. He also co-founded Justice Democrats in 2017 and ran a long-shot bid of his own for the 2024 Democratic presidential nomination. His Rebellion PAC sparked controversy during the 2026 midterms with an ad tying U.S. funding for Israel to higher grocery prices, which the campaign of then-Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed distanced itself from.
Uygur, who was also a prominent backer of Vermont independent Sen. Bernie Sanders' presidential runs, has a blunt prediction for 2028: "I'm positive Ro Khanna is going to win."
body_zh: 罗·卡纳（Ro Khanna）尚未发起 2028 年竞选，但他已经拥有了一位民粹主义先锋。
进步煽动者岑克·维吾尔将于周四晚上在侄子哈桑·派克 (Hasan Piker) 的 Twitch 直播节目中正式支持这位加州民主党人，这场感恩节辩论马拉松被两人称为“Cenksgiving”。维吾尔告诉《政治》杂志，他将把卡纳视为最好的民粹主义进步候选人。他的 Rebellion PAC 也将于周四晚首次推出 2028 年首个广告，宣传卡纳的候选资格。
“对我来说，这是理所当然的，”维古尔在接受采访时说道，并解释了他支持卡纳的原因。 “你还会支持谁，为什么进步主义者或民粹主义者会支持其他人？”
除了政治行动委员会对卡纳的支持外，维吾尔还推出了自己的“Draft Ro”网站，以收集签名并展示其他早期高调的代言人，尽管他尚未透露是谁。
此次认可是 2028 年周期的首批认可之一，而且是在任何主要候选人正式宣布之前进行的。在华盛顿内部，卡纳的机会被认为相当渺茫。但对于维吾尔族来说，这种低估正是吸引力的一部分。
“我喜欢它，”维吾尔谈到怀疑论时说道。 “如果华盛顿有人支持他，我就不会支持他。”
“我们正在对抗华盛顿，”他补充道。 “因此，如果华盛顿不喜欢某个候选人，那就完美了。”
维吾尔将他的支持与他试图为 2028 年进步人士制定的试金石结合起来：候选人必须称以色列在加沙的所作所为是种族灭绝，并支持结束美国对以色列的资助。 “这实际上与以色列无关，”维吾尔说。 “问题在于：这个人是否会代表我们？”
他说，卡纳是“极少数，也许是唯一能够通过这项测试的候选人之一。”他也考虑到了另一个：“还有AOC。如果她参选，那就是另一个可以通过测试的人了。”
但赞美也仅此而已。他对卡纳的支持之际，许多其他进步人士都在观望众议员亚历山大·奥卡西奥-科尔特斯（纽约州民主党）是否加入。维吾尔人不是其中之一。当被问及她的加入是否会改变他的计算时，他说：“不会改变 1%。”
“抱歉，但我认为 AOC 不是这个意思，”他说。 “我认为她不会做她所说的任何事情，所以我不会支持那些不会兑现承诺的人。”
“她痴迷于当权者，所以她将进行一场软弱的竞选，”他补充道。 “她想让民主党领导人和主流媒体高兴。祝这个策略好运。”
卡纳告诉《政治》杂志，他计划在假期后决定是否参选，奥卡西奥-科尔特斯是否参选不会影响他的决定。

维吾尔人的支持可能会给这位潜在的 2028 年候选人在民粹主义左翼中获得一些可信度，更不用说维吾尔人于 2002 年推出的历史最悠久、最受欢迎的网络进步节目之一《青年土耳其党》的推动。他还在 2017 年共同创办了正义民主党，并以自己的方式竞选 2024 年民主党总统提名。他的叛乱政治行动委员会在 2026 年中期选举期间因一则广告将美国对以色列的资助与更高的杂货价格挂钩而引发争议，当时的参议院候选人阿卜杜勒·赛义德的竞选团队与这一广告保持了距离。
维吾尔也是佛蒙特州独立参议员伯尼·桑德斯 (Bernie Sanders) 总统竞选的重要支持者，他对 2028 年做出了直率的预测：“我确信罗·卡纳 (Ro Khanna) 将获胜。”
